name: Anger
description: Deal ^6 damage. Place a copy of this card in your discard pile.
descriptionplus: Deal ^8 damage. Place a copy of this card in your discard pile.
statement: An okay pick for act one, particularly when you are planning to fight the gremlin nob. Can help against enemies that pollute your deck, such as Hexaghost and the Sentries. In later acts, can cause you to have turns where you are unable to use all of your energy which is an ineffective use of your turn.

name: Armaments
description: Gain 5 Block. Upgrade ^a ^card in your hand for the rest of combat.
descriptionplus: Gain 5 Block. Upgrade ^ALL cards in your hand for the rest of combat.
statement: Armaments can be a very powerful card to upgrade first, as it likely has a lot of un-upgraded cards that it can hit throughout act 1. If Armaments makes any card that you wanted to play at least 1 energy cheaper, then it has already paid for itself. Even stronger if you can manage to couple it with some draw effects so it's hitting as many cards as possible. Can also be good in large decks where you don't have the opportunity to upgrade your whole deck.

name: Barricade
description: Block no longer expires at the start of your turn.
descriptionplus: Block no longer expires at the start of your turn.
statement: A very powerful win condition if you are able to draft big blocks with it, but due to its high cost it can fall flat in decks that don't support it. Entrench is a must-have pairing for longer fights.

name: Bash
description: Deal ^8 damage. Apply ^2 Vulnerable.
descriptionplus: Deal ^10 damage. Apply ^3 Vulnerable.
statement: Ironclad's bread and butter, Bash doesn't need to be removed from the deck as vulnerable works well with many of his strength synergies. Usually only consider upgrading if you don't have additional sources of vulnerable.

name: Battle Trance
description: Draw ^3 cards. You cannot draw additional cards this turn.
descriptionplus: Draw ^4 cards. You cannot draw additional cards this turn.
statement: Fantastic card, strong in many decks whether you have high energy or not. Be aware of its anti-draw effect. For this reason, drafting more than two battle trances in one deck can clutter your hand.

name: Berserk
description: Gain ^2 vulnerable. At the start of your turn, gain 1 [energy].
descriptionplus: Gain ^1 vulnerable. At the start of your turn, gain 1 [energy].
statement: Very powerful card, this is basically the equivalent of an energy relic in card form. Note that the vulnerability starts on this turn, meaning that unupgraded you are vulnerable this turn and next, and upgraded you are only vulnerable for this turn.

name: Blood for Blood
description: Costs 1 less [energy] for each time you lose HP in combat. Deal ^18 damage.
descriptionplus: Costs 1 less [energy] for each time you lose HP in combat. Deal ^22 damage.
statement: Too slow to be reliable, and generally speaking you do not want to be taking this much damage in fights. It acts as more of a consolation prize. Intentionally tanking one damage when blocking can improve the effectiveness of this card. For obvious reasons, intangible synergises very well.

name: Bloodletting
description: Lose 3 HP. Gain [energy] [energy].
descriptionplus: Lose 3 HP. Gain [energy] [energy] [energy].
statement: Strong as long as you have the cards draw to be able to make the most of all of the energy that you gain. Best when paired with some healing effects, as it is easy to slowly bleed out over the course of your run.

name: Bludgeon
description: Deal ^32 damage.
descriptionplus: Deal ^42 damage.
statement: A solid damage card early when it can one shot enemies. Its high cost can leave you open to counter attacks as you are usually unable to block on the same turn. Brilliant with damage amplifying effects.

name: Body Slam
description: Deal damage equal to your current Block.
descriptionplus: Deal damage equal to your current Block.
statement: Body Slam can be a game winning card and is a staple in the Barricade deck archetype. At 0 energy this becomes even more effective as it usually allows you to play one more block card before using it. Remember that this card’s damage is also increased by strength so even with 0 block it can do damage.

name: Brutality
description: At the start of your turn, lose 1 HP and draw 1 card.
descriptionplus: ^Innate. At the start of your turn, lose 1 HP and draw 1 card.
statement: Be wary of the amount of damage that you can accumulate when using Brutality. It is recommended that you take this card with some other form of healing. This card is exceptionally powerful with Rupture, as it also grants you one strength per turn. On some slow fights, playing this will not be worth it.

name: Burning Pact
description: Exhaust 1 card. Draw ^2 cards.
descriptionplus: Exhaust 1 card. Draw ^3 cards.
statement: Used to thin decks, only valuable once you have the energy to use this. Can be used to burn curses in certain scenarios, but remember the card must be exhausted before drawing takes place. If this is the last card in your hand, it doesn't exhaust anything.

name: Carnage
description: Ethereal. Deal ^20 damage.
descriptionplus: Ethereal. Deal ^28 damage.
statement: Carnage is a powerful card with very few downsides. I would definitely recommend this card early on in the run and later on it can do well as a solid source of damage if running a defensive deck. The ethereal nature of this card is almost completely irrelevant, as it is rarely a win condition and there are other ways of ending a fight.

name: Clash
description: Can only be played if every card in your hand is an Attack. Deal ^14 damage.
descriptionplus: Can only be played if every card in your hand is an Attack. Deal ^18 damage.
statement: Although this card is powerful on earlier ascensions, as soon as Ascender’s Bane starts appearing in the deck this card becomes extremely unreliable. In theory, clash can be played so long as you play out the other skills and powers in your hand, but in practice this is often clunky, not optimal, or too expensive, and curses and status cards are often impossible to play out.

name: Cleave
description: Deal ^8 damage to ALL enemies.
descriptionplus: Deal ^11 damage to ALL enemies.
statement: A solid AOE card but nothing special. I would recommend picking at least 1 multi target attack by the end of act 1.

name: Clothesline
description: Deal ^12 damage. Apply ^2 Weak.
descriptionplus: Deal ^14 damage. Apply ^3 Weak.
statement: A solid and consistent source of weak for ironclad that does not exhaust, making it a common pick in many decks. Less effective against enemies with artifact due to its high cost.

name: Combust
description: At the end of your turn, lose 1 HP and deal ^5 damage to ALL enemies.
descriptionplus: At the end of your turn, lose 1 HP and deal ^7 damage to ALL enemies.
statement: Generally this card is not as effective as it first seems, since its aoe effect is often to its detriment: typically, you want to kill enemies one by one in quick succession rather than slowly whittling them all down at the same time. it is easy for the health loss to stack up over time, particularly during longer encounters and boss fights. On the other hand, this is good versus enemies who apply the weak debuff or have other forms of attack damage mitigation, such as the byrds. This card is exceptionally powerful with Rupture, as it also grants you one strength per turn.

name: Corruption
description: Skills cost 0. Whenever you play a Skill, Exhaust it.
descriptionplus: Skills cost 0. Whenever you play a Skill, Exhaust it.
statement: This card is an exceptionally powerful win condition, but it is also a risky strategy. Corruption is powerful on the first time through your deck but once your deck is reshuffled and all of your defensive capabilities have been exhausted the fights can become scary. This is why it is very important to be careful how early you cast corruption, particularly in fights that you expect to be long such as boss battles. This card in combination with dead branch is one of the most insane combos in the entire game, as each skill that you exhaust has a chance of generating another free skill and so on and so forth. I typically recommend running one or two Iron Waves in this deck just in case a fight just go longer than you expect it to and you still need a source of block. Barricade can also work very well with corruption as the block that you accumulate does not expire right away. Dark Embrace can lead to cycling your first deck shuffle very quickly too, for better or for worse, and Feel No Pain amps up the block gain.

name: Dark Embrace
description: Whenever a card is Exhausted, draw 1 card.
descriptionplus: Whenever a card is Exhausted, draw 1 card.
statement: Dark embrace is usually only picked in conjunction with corruption. In theory it is possible to get value out of this power through cards that exhaust themselves or other cards but the payoff is rarely worth it.

name: Defend
description: Gain ^5 Block.
descriptionplus: Gain ^8 Block.

name: Demon Form
description: At the start of each turn, gain ^2 Strength.
descriptionplus: At the start of each turn, gain ^3 Strength.
statement: Absolutely game winning in boss fights. Picking one is always a good idea, more than one is usually excessive. Goes great with Limit Break and Heavy Blade. Not always suitable for hallway fights.

name: Disarm
description: Enemy loses ^2 Strength. Exhaust.
descriptionplus: Enemy loses ^3 Strength. Exhaust.
statement: An exceptionally powerful defensive option in ironclad who doesn't usually have that many. Turns certain encounters into a joke, such as the plant, Hexaghost and the Heart to some extent. Picking one or two of these is never wrong.

name: Double Tap
description: This turn, your next ^Attack is played twice.
descriptionplus: This turn, your next ^2 ^Attacks are played twice.
statement: Double tap is typically much more effective on expensive attacks, since the second time it is played it is played for free. Obvious choices are bludgeon, searing blow, and carnage. Cards that apply vulnerable benefit from the damage boost on the second play. This card can also get greater value out of Reaper. Also synergises with relics that work based on attacks played, such as Shuriken, Kunai, Pen Nib, etc.

name: Dropkick
description: Deal 5 damage. If the target is Vulnerable, gain [energy] and draw 1 card.
descriptionplus: Deal ^8 damage. If the target is Vulnerable, gain [energy] and draw 1 card.
statement: A lot of the time, this card is worse than a strike - and even at its best, it's only 5 free damage. Can work if you have 3 or more ways of applying vulnerable, but otherwise often underperforms. Decks that build around this mechanic do exist with multiple copies of dropkick for fast free cycling, but this strategy struggles against the Time-Eater (12 turns), Deca and Donu (Artifacts) and the Heart (damage per card played).

name: Dual Wield
description: Create ^a ^copy of an Attack or Power card in your hand.
descriptionplus: Create ^2 ^copies of an Attack or Power card in your hand.
statement: Dual wield typically works well with either cheap cards or by duplicating your wind conditions. For example, adding additional copies of a supercharged searing blow to your deck can make boss fights a breeze. Additionally, this card can be good with free attacks, as often if you are copying a card that costs more than 1 energy you wouldn't be able to play all of them in the same turn anyway. For this reason, it can work quite well with dropkick given that the enemy is already vulnerable. Of course, this card also works on powers, although some powers such as corruption do not benefit from being played again. Metallicize, fire breathing and rupture are some of the best power candidates. Note that any discounts on the original card apply to the copies as well.

name: Entrench
description: Double your current Block.
descriptionplus: Double your current Block.
statement: Entrench on its own is typically a terrible card. Very commonly you end up with no block options in hand and entrench therefore offers 0 block, and even when it does hit it typically provides 5 block for 2 energy – a terrible deal. This card DOES however have the potential to be insanely powerful when combined with barricade. I would never take this card unless I already had barricade or was working towards a barricade archetype.

name: Evolve
description: Whenever you draw a Status, draw ^1 card.
descriptionplus: Whenever you draw a Status, draw ^2 cards.
statement: Though niche, this card has the power to render certain battles laughable. The dazes from the Sentries elite and the Chosen's Hex debuff are nullified. It makes the downside of pollute cards (that add statuses to your deck) negligible. Even in fights where it does nothing, it can be simply played for 1 energy to exhaust it or in shorter fights it can simply be ignored.

name: Exhume
description: Choose an Exhausted card and put it in your hand. Exhaust.
descriptionplus: Choose an Exhausted card and put it in your hand. Exhaust.
statement: The power of exhume depends entirely on your exhaust cards. It can be powerful with Reaper to maximise healing or with feed to maximise HP gain, although finding the ideal scenario to pull this off is difficult. Note that you cannot exhume an exhume for infinite combos. Note that this can also bring back an important card that got exhausted by something like a Fiend Fire.

name: Feed
description: Deal ^10 damage. If Fatal, raise your Max HP by ^3&#46 Exhaust.
descriptionplus: Deal ^12 damage. If Fatal, raise your Max HP by ^4&#46 Exhaust.
statement: The earlier you take this card the better. Can be game-winning if you are able to stack it consistently. Consider stalling non-threatening hallway fights to get another Feed proc if you can do so without taking damage.

name: Feel No Pain
description: Whenever a card is Exhausted, gain ^3 Block.
descriptionplus: Whenever a card is Exhausted, gain ^4 Block.
statement: A card that synergises very well with corruption, but without it tends to fall flat. The extra occasional block from this effect can work in a deck that has a few standard exhausting cards, but this strategy rarely scales into the late game without huge sources of exhaust. Note that ethereal cards trigger this effect too.

name: Fiend Fire
description: Exhaust your hand. Deal ^7 damage for each Exhausted card. Exhaust.
descriptionplus: Exhaust your hand. Deal ^10 damage for each Exhausted card. Exhaust.
statement: A great source of fast damage. Ideal for corridor fights, but can leave you without important cards in longer elite or boss fights. Bonus points if your deck synergises with exhaust.

name: Fire Breathing
description: Whenever you draw a Status or Curse card, deal ^6 damage to ALL enemies.
descriptionplus: Whenever you draw a Status or Curse card, deal ^10 damage to ALL enemies.
statement: Running one copy of fire breathing is usually enough to hard counter certain fights without posing too much of a disadvantage in fights where it is useless. This power is also a build-around card and can be picked with cards that pollute your deck, such as second wind, wild strike, and reckless charge to make it powerful in any encounter. It also makes curses less of a drawback.

name: Flame Barrier
description: Gain ^12 Block. Whenever you are attacked this turn, deal ^4 damage to the attacker.
descriptionplus: Gain ^16 Block. Whenever you are attacked this turn, deal ^6 damage to the attacker.
statement: One of ironclads best block cards, flame barrier is a solid amount of block with the potential to deal moderate damage. A well-timed flame barrier can destroy the birds, is powerful versus the Hexaghost and in the right situation can deal up to 90 damage to the Heart in one turn.

name: Flex
description: Gain ^2 Strength. At the end of your turn, lose ^2 Strength.
descriptionplus: Gain ^4 Strength. At the end of your turn, lose ^4 Strength.
statement: Although flex seems to perform well in lower ascensions, it lacks the value required to compete at higher ascensions. If drawn without any attacks in hand, it is effectively useless. It must affect 3 attacks in order to be better than Anger, which is easier said than done in ironclad. What's more, the strength debuff that it applies can consume your artifact stacks, which is usually a bad thing although in some instances using it to permanently gain 4 strength can be powerful.

name: Ghostly Armor
description: Ethereal. Gain ^10 Block.
descriptionplus: Ethereal. Gain ^13 Block.
statement: This is a high-value, solid block card for ironclad and its ethereal nature is rarely relevant.

name: Havoc
description: Play the top card of your draw pile and Exhaust it.
descriptionplus: Play the top card of your draw pile and Exhaust it.
statement: Havoc is an extremely dangerous card. Although it has the potential to high roll and play expensive and powerful cards for zero energy, the fact that you do not get to pick the targets for the attack makes the card much worse. Furthermore, havoc exhausts the card, which means your win condition such as a supercharged searing blow could be exhausted. Other times, you might accidentally hit an enemy with thorns, accidentally reach a certain health threshold on a specific boss, or even accidentally exhaust your entire hand. Having a run end due to Havoc is extremely saddening. Cards such as warcry and headbutt allow you to choose which card havoc triggers, assuming you draw one of these cards alongside havoc and the card that you want is either in your discard pile or also in your hand (if this sounds unlikely to happen, it’s because it is). Note that X cost cards do not actually use any energy.

name: Headbutt
description: Deal ^9 damage. Place a card from your discard pile on top of your draw pile.
descriptionplus: Deal ^12 damage. Place a card from your discard pile on top of your draw pile.
statement: Best suited to bigger decks, as you have a larger pool of cards to choose from on average.

name: Heavy Blade
description: Deal 14 damage. Strength affects Heavy Blade ^3 times.
descriptionplus: Deal 14 damage. Strength affects Heavy Blade ^5 times.
statement: Heavy blade gets the highest value out of strength for any ironclad card except for pummel. pommels disadvantage however is that it exhausts. A very solid card in strength decks, but I would not recommend this card before finding any strength cards or relics as at 2 energy it underperforms.

name: Hemokinesis
description: Lose ^2 HP. Deal ^15 damage.
descriptionplus: Lose ^2 HP. Deal ^20 damage.
statement: Despite this card's high damage, it is very easy to slowly bleed out throughout the course of a run if you're not careful. In many scenarios, this card is able to kill an enemy before they attack, effectively reducing the amount of health you would lose overall. However it performs much worse against bosses with high health totals that require many attacks to kill. Obviously, this card synergises well with the likes of Rupture. Tungsten can also be useful in preventing damage.

name: Immolate
description: Deal ^21 damage to ALL enemies. Shuffle a Burn into your discard pile.
descriptionplus: Deal ^28 damage to ALL enemies. Shuffle a Burn into your discard pile.
statement: Immolate is a really powerful attack for hallway fights. It has very high aoe damage and is capable of killing multiple foes in one turn. the burn card goes into your discard pile so in many fights you are unlikely to even draw it before the encounter is over. This card is less effective versus single target enemies with high health totals and against bosses, as the burns will add up , deal damage to you and begin cluttering your hand. This card stops being as effective in act 3 but can carry runs if picked up early.

name: Impervious
description: Gain ^30 Block. Exhaust.
descriptionplus: Gain ^40 Block. Exhaust.
statement: Impervious is a powerful card, And I would normally pick it over skipping, but often there are better rare cards in ironclad. it can save a run from time to time if it is drawn on the right turn. Can be very useful versus the heart. This card is at its best in a barricade deck, as often the block is slightly overkill and barricade ensures that impervious always hits maximum value.

name: Infernal Blade
description: Add a random Attack to your hand. It costs 0 this turn. Exhaust.
descriptionplus: Add a random Attack to your hand. It costs 0 this turn. Exhaust.
statement: This is a card that I would only really consider taking on act one. it is very unreliable and later on in a run when you have higher energy you might find that you are ending the turn with energy to spare when you draw this card. The power of the card lies in its ability to create an expensive attack such as bludgeon and allow you to play it for free. The worst case scenarios for this card are hardly terrible, but its unpredictable nature makes it a liability and often times you would be better with a leaner deck.

name: Inflame
description: Gain ^2 Strength.
descriptionplus: Gain ^3 Strength.
statement: Inflame is a very solid power. It allows you to lean into a strength deck without fully committing (unlike limit break by contrast) and strength is relevant to every single ironclad deck (with the exception of Juggernaut, perhaps). It is cheap, easily played and good value.

name: Intimidate
description: Apply ^1 Weak to ALL enemies. Exhaust.
descriptionplus: Apply ^2 Weak to ALL enemies. Exhaust.
statement: Intimidate is a fine early pick, as it gives ironclad a defensive option that does not require any energy. However, the fact that it only applies 1 weak means that drawing it on a turn where the enemy is not attacking makes it a pointless draw, and since it exhausts it’s not reliable for longer fights. You will need an additional source of weak later on.

name: Iron Wave
description: Gain ^5 Block. Deal ^5 damage.
descriptionplus: Gain ^7 Block. Deal ^7 damage.
statement: Iron wave is decent early on, for example versus the Louse encounter. It is okay as a filler card as it is fairly high value but it's nothing special. Can be used in Corruption decks as a source of block once all your skills have been exhausted. This card uniquely benefits from both strength and dexterity and can slot into Kunai/Shuriken decks well.

name: Juggernaut
description: Whenever you gain Block, deal ^5 damage to a random enemy.
descriptionplus: Whenever you gain Block, deal ^7 damage to a random enemy.
statement: This card can serve as a builder round win condition in very specific decks, although it might struggle versus certain encounters. The hex debuff in particular is very difficult to work with in a deck with mostly skills. Is it worth mentioning that this card works very well with Metallicize and any form of plated armor. This power can be run in conjunction with a barricade deck although it is not strictly necessary. More often than not however, the fact that the damage is random can make it difficult to reliably finish targets off and the damage does not scale with vulnerable which can be too slow in many fights.

name: Limit Break
description: Double your Strength. ^Exhaust.
descriptionplus: Double your Strength.
statement: In the right decks, can lead to insane amounts of damage; however, without any strength cards to support it this card is as good as a curse. Doubling 1 strength isn't even enough justification to play this card. Never pick this without any form of strength gain.

name: Metallicize
description: At the end of your turn, gain ^3 Block.
descriptionplus: At the end of your turn, gain ^4 Block.
statement: This card is solid as it provides a lot of value over time, though it is nothing to write home about. It does not serve as a win condition, but it will likely prevent around 15 damage in a normal fight which is strong for its energy cost. Stacking Metallicize can be a strong strategy, meaning that your second and third copy of this card are actually more valuable than the first. The continuously stacking block works well with barricade, although it does not rely on it, and it also synergises well with plated armour. Generally pick it early or not at all.

name: Offering
description: Lose 6 HP. Gain [energy] [energy]. Draw ^3 cards. Exhaust.
descriptionplus: Lose 6 HP. Gain [energy] [energy]. Draw ^5 cards. Exhaust.
statement: Offering is a card with a very powerful effect but a pretty huge downside. Although it provides a lot of options through its additional draw and energy gain, it completely negates the healing that you get from your relic. As long as the effect is preventing you from taking six damage in the long room, for example by providing additional energy for block or by ensuring a monster is dead before it deals a high damaging attack, then you are using this card effectively. I would generally recommend having at least one additional source of healing to make this card worth the risk. It is possible to abstain from playing it uncertain fights that are low threat, but this usually feels terrible as ironclad doesn't typically have many options for drawing anyway.

name: Perfected Strike
description: Deal 6 damage. Deals an additional ^+2 damage for ALL of your cards containing "Strike".
descriptionplus: Deal 6 damage. Deals an additional ^+3 damage for ALL of your cards containing "Strike".
statement: I would only consider taking this card on the first half of act one. As a base, it is 18 damage for 2 energy which is about average value. This is okay early but must be built around in the later stages of the game to remain relevant, or else removed. Perfected strike decks often end up with around 40 cards in, meaning that your draw can become quite unreliable. If playing a perfected strike deck, you should take all other perfected strikes that are offered as well. Consider running Headbutts to pull it back as many times as possible. This strategy is inconsistent and I would not recommend it at high ascension.

name: Pommel Strike
description: Deal ^9 damage. Draw ^1 card.
descriptionplus: Deal ^10 damage. Draw ^2 cards.
statement: Pommel strike is a filler card which I would pick in situations where I am lacking draw after having gained at least one form of energy relic. Until you have extra energy, the draw is usually pointless.

name: Power Through
description: Add 2 Wounds to your hand. Gain ^15 Block.
descriptionplus: Add 2 Wounds to your hand. Gain ^20 Block.
statement: Power through exists as a defensive option that synergises with pollute decks. For this reason it synergises decently well with Fire Breathing. I typically would not pick this card without any pollute synergies, since the two wounds can quickly clutter a deck. Evolve can be used to offset the pollute effect but be aware that it is possible to have a hand with 10 cards in, most of which are wounds. as a caveat, since the wounds are directly added to your hand they can be used with Fiend Fire or Second Wind as additional fuel.

name: Pummel
description: Deal 2 damage ^4 times. Exhaust.
descriptionplus: Deal 2 damage ^5 times. Exhaust.
statement: Great for dealing with byrds at the start of Act 2. Most commonly sees play in a strength deck. Since this card exhausts, it cannot be considered a reliable win condition for longer fights in decks that are built around stacking strength.

name: Rage
description: Whenever you play an Attack this turn, gain ^3 Block.
descriptionplus: Whenever you play an Attack this turn, gain ^5 Block.
statement: Rage, like flex, is a fairly inconsistent card. On its own, it does nothing, and in a typical hand it may only provide 9 block. I would definitely not recommend this card at high ascensions, but if you are on a low ascension and you find that you have a very aggressive deck with not many sources of block then this can act as a band-aid and save you.

name: Rampage
description: Deal 8 damage. Every time this card is played, increase its damage by ^5 for this combat.
descriptionplus: Deal 8 damage. Every time this card is played, increase its damage by ^8 for this combat.
statement: Can be a win condition if the deck focuses on replaying this card repeatedly, but this strategy is inconsistent at higher ascension. Best in slim decks or decks that exhaust. Can be a useful tool against Hexaghost for example if your deck is low on dps.

name: Reaper
description: Deal ^4 damage to ALL enemies&#46 Heal for unblocked damage. Exhaust.
descriptionplus: Deal ^5 damage to ALL enemies&#46 Heal for unblocked damage. Exhaust.
statement: Reaper is an incredibly powerful card, and possibly one of ironclad’s strongest. Without any support, the healing that it does is fairly negligible, however its damage and healing is increased by vulnerable and as soon as you start stacking strength this card becomes incredibly strong. It's possible to heal upwards of 50 health in one combat in the right situation. It is not always correct to play repair on the turn that you draw it - sometimes you want to wait for more procs of Demon Form or your Limit Break. Keep in mind that Reaper can only heal for damage done - overkill does not heal you for the excess amount.

name: Reckless Charge
description: Deal ^7 damage. Shuffle a Dazed into your draw pile.
descriptionplus: Deal ^10 damage. Shuffle a Dazed into your draw pile.
statement: Reckless Charge can be a good pick in act 1 when 0 energy cards are more valuable, and also when the dazed effect does not typically stop you from using all of your energy every turn. This card’s downside can be used to its advantage when running a pollute deck with powers like Fire Breathing and Evolve. Don't forget that the ethereal dazed card will also exhaust itself at the end of the turn, which can trigger exhaust bonuses from relics like Charon’s Ashes.

name: Rupture
description: Whenever you lose HP from a card, gain 1 Strength.
descriptionplus: Whenever you lose HP from a card, gain 2 Strength.
statement: Rupture is a slow but steady source of strength when combined with powers such as combust and brutality. It also works with curse damage (to great effect with Pain) and burn damage. I would never pick this card without having a single source of self damage already, and ideally you have two or three. The main benefit to this card is that it is inexpensive 1 compared to something like demon form; however demon form is much more reliable, consistent and does not require support from other cards. Be aware that Tungsten Rod can prevent all damage from Combust and Brutality, preventing strength gain.

name: Searing Blow
description: Deal ^12 damage. Can be upgraded any number of times.
descriptionplus: Deal ^16 damage. Can be upgraded any number of times.
statement: Can be a winning card if the deck focuses on upgrading this card almost exclusively. Each upgrade provides a bigger bonus than the last. Should be played in small decks to get as many plays as possible. Be aware that almost every single upgrade will be dedicated to this card, so don't pick cards that are only valuable when upgraded (such as True Grit).

name: Second Wind
description: Exhaust all non-Attack cards in your hand and gain ^5 Block for each.
descriptionplus: Exhaust all non-Attack cards in your hand and gain ^7 Block for each.
statement: This card can be difficult to use as it can put you in situations where you have to choose between taking damage and exhausting key cards (such as a Demon Form). Remember that you can play cards that you don't want to be exhausted, as long as you have the energy and don't need the additional block. This card can work well in a pollute deck with the likes of Power Through as it is very effective at removing wounds and burns from your deck, although this strategy can be fairly unreliable without strong draw cards. Needless to say, this card pairs very well with Dead Branch, like all other exhaust strategies, and fits very well into exhaust-focused decks that run powers like Feel No Pain and Dark Embrace.

name: Seeing Red
description: Gain [energy] [energy]. Exhaust.
descriptionplus: Gain [energy] [energy]. Exhaust.
statement: A solid energy card which is rare for ironclad. Ironclad has very expensive attacks when compared to other classes so it is not normally difficult to get full value out of this card. The more sources of energy you have, the less powerful this card becomes, which makes it a strong early pick but its effectiveness tends to drop off without strong sources of draw. Pairs well with Ice Cream for obvious reasons.

name: Sentinel
description: Gain ^5 Block. If this card is Exhausted, gain [energy] [energy].
descriptionplus: Gain ^8 Block. If this card is Exhausted, gain [energy] [energy] [energy].
statement: Only ever pick this if you have Corruption.

name: Sever Soul
description: Exhaust all non-Attack cards in your hand. Deal ^16 damage.
descriptionplus: Exhaust all non-Attack cards in your hand. Deal ^20 damage.
statement: Sever Soul is a strong source of damage for its energy cost with few downsides. Be careful not to exhaust key cards in your deck, for example a Demon Form, although playing these cards before Sever Soul saves them from being exhausted so long as you have the energy. This card can work well in a pollute deck with the likes of Power Through as it is very effective at removing wounds and burns from your deck, although this strategy can be fairly unreliable without strong draw cards. Needless to say, this card pairs very well with Dead Branch, like all other exhaust strategies, and fits very well into exhaust-focused decks that run powers like Feel No Pain and Dark Embrace.

name: Shockwave
description: Apply ^3 Weak and Vulnerable to ALL enemies. Exhaust
descriptionplus: Apply ^5 Weak and Vulnerable to ALL enemies. Exhaust
statement: Although expensive, the shockwave played early in combat can debuff enemies long enough to ensure most are dead by the end of its duration, and to mitigate damage until then. A decent card, and a good substitute for Uppercut and Clothesline where necessary. Can be hard to play this card with just 3 energy, so energy gain is recommended.

name: Shrug It Off
description: Gain ^8 Block. Draw 1 card.
descriptionplus: Gain ^11 Block. Draw 1 card.
statement: Although Shrug It Off is a common card, it is extremely reliable, offering a decent source of block and draw in a class that doesn't have much of either, making it very valuable. It is a typical to finish a run with three copies of this card.

name: Spot Weakness
description: If an enemy intends to attack, gain ^3 Strength.
descriptionplus: If an enemy intends to attack, gain ^4 Strength.
statement: Spot weakness is a decent source of instant strength and its conditions are easily met. The benefit of spot weakness is that it can be played multiple times in a single fight, unlike Inflame. Demon forms strength gain is more consistent, but also slower and more expensive, making spot weakness more effective in hallway fights. In practice, if you are running a strength deck, you will likely be running a combination of all of these cards.

name: Strike
description: Deal ^6 damage.
descriptionplus: Deal ^9 damage.

name: Sword Boomerang
description: Deal 3 damage to a random enemy ^3 times.
descriptionplus: Deal 3 damage to a random enemy ^4 times.
statement: Sword Boomerang is only to be picked in strength decks. Be aware that you do not choose Sword Boomerang’s targets which can make this very unreliable and frustrating. This card becomes supercharged with enough strength, so much so that you can finish off hordes of enemies with a single use, offsetting its randomness. A fair substitute for Heavy Blade, though usually slightly worse.

name: Thunderclap
description: Deal ^4 damage and apply 1 Vulnerable to ALL enemies.
descriptionplus: Deal ^7 damage and apply 1 Vulnerable to ALL enemies.
statement: Thunderclap is a fairly unremarkable card due to the fact that it only applies 1 vulnerable. It has unimpressive damage and is only powerful when paired with another aoe card on the same turn, which can be hard to execute. Be aware that Thunderclap can work with cards like bash by extending the duration of vulnerable without requiring damage on the same turn. Strength can also greatly increase the effectiveness of this card.

name: True Grit
description: Gain ^7 Block. Exhaust ^a ^random ^card from your hand.
descriptionplus: Gain ^9 Block. Exhaust ^a ^card from your hand.
statement: True Grit is another strong source of block for the ironclad, and the selective exhaust ability is not to be underestimated. It can be used to remove curses or status cards from your hand, or even remove niche cards that are not relevant to this encounter (such as an Evolve) or just generally low value (Strikes and Defends). Note that this card must be upgraded for you to be able to choose which card is exhausted, and as such it is highly recommended that this card is upgraded if selected. Slight exhaust synergy.

name: Twin Strike
description: Deal ^5 damage twice.
descriptionplus: Deal ^7 damage twice.
statement: Twin strike is an okay card which can provide some DPS in the early game whilst also being able to lean into the strength archetype without committing to it. It is an important card against the byrds and I recommend picking up at least one source of multihit in act 1, whether or not you're running a strength deck.

name: Uppercut
description: Deal 13 damage. Apply ^1 Weak. Apply ^1 Vulnerable.
descriptionplus: Deal 13 damage. Apply ^2 Weak. Apply ^2 Vulnerable.
statement: Uppercut is a potent debuff card which can be effective against single target encounters. It is difficult to make use of the vulnerable proc on the same turn, and it is therefore recommended that you upgrade this card. Uppercut is a good substitute for Clothesline.

name: Warcry
description: Draw ^a ^card. Place a card from your hand on top of your draw pile. Exhaust.
descriptionplus: Draw ^2 cards. Place a card from your hand on top of your draw pile. Exhaust.
statement: This card is intended to be used to make your current turn and the next turn have better options. It synergises well with Havoc, since you can control which card is played and exhausted. You might think that this card has no possible downsides since it is free and draws, but enemies like the Chosen, the Time-Eater and the Heart make Warcry a less valuable pick. For this reason, I would not generally recommend picking one except perhaps early. As a side-note, warcry can be used in combination with Fire Breathing to draw and re-shuffle curses and statuses into your deck.

name: Whirlwind
description: Deal ^5 damage to ALL enemies X times.
descriptionplus: Deal ^8 damage to ALL enemies X times.
statement: Whirlwind is a decent and reliable card as it allows you to spend all of your energy on the turn that you draw it (except against a spiker perhaps). It also scales incredibly well with strength. Since it is X cost, it can be played with 0 energy to proc certain relics, such as Kunai and Shuriken. Overall a very reliable card with potential upsides.

name: Wild Strike
description: Deal ^12 damage. Shuffle a Wound into your draw pile.
descriptionplus: Deal ^17 damage. Shuffle a Wound into your draw pile.
statement: Without any pollute synergies, I would consider taking wild strike perhaps on act 1, where even on turns where you draw a wound you are still able to spend all of your energy. It is a lot of fast damage making it useful in corridor fights, although the wounds can stack up if you have no way of dealing with them. This is why it's best to take wild strike in a deck that to make the most of pollution, such as one with Fire Breathing and Evolve.

name: A Thousand Cuts
description: Whenever you play a card, deal ^1 damage to ALL enemies.
descriptionplus: Whenever you play a card, deal ^2 damage to ALL enemies.
statement: A Thousand Cuts is a strong source of aoe damage for shiv decks, since shivs are typically single target focused. It can also be played in an infinite cycle discard deck as the only source of damage, although the Time-Eater and the Heart counter this strategy enormously. When upgraded, the damage is not too bad, however its high cost can make it difficult to play. This card is best in encounters where smaller mobs are continuously spawned, such as the gremlins elite in act 2.

name: Accuracy
description: Shivs deal ^4 additional damage.
descriptionplus: Shivs deal ^6 additional damage.
statement: Accuracy is an all or nothing card. If you are running a shiv deck and you expect to beat the heart at ascension 20, you must normally run at least one Accuracy. The time-eater greatly counters shiv decks and accuracy allows each card to be worth playing. The same goes for the heart. I would never pick accuracy unless the deck's win condition was solely shivs.

name: Acrobatics
description: Draw ^3 cards. Discard 1 card.
descriptionplus: Draw ^4 cards. Discard 1 card.
statement: This card is a solid source of draw with a tiny bit of discard synergy. a couple of copies of this can help ensure do you get the drawers that you need when you need them. I tend to pick up acrobatics in act two or three after having picked up an energy relic. This card is particularly good at finding curses and throwing them in the discard pile.

name: Adrenaline
description: Gain [energy]. Draw 2 cards. Exhaust.
descriptionplus: Gain [energy] [energy]. Draw 2 cards. Exhaust.
statement: Adrenaline is an extremely powerful card and an insta pick in almost every scenario. I don't think it's possible to have too many copies. It allows you to quickly complete the first cycle of your deck, offsetting the odds of not drawing your key cards that could be buried towards the bottom. Pairs very well with Bottled Lightning.

name: After Image
description: Whenever you play a card, gain 1 Block.
descriptionplus: ^Innate. Whenever you play a card, gain 1 Block.
statement: After Image is one of the Silent’s many extremely powerful block options. The first copy is great, and every copy of After Image that you add beyond that just makes it better and better. This deck has obvious synergies with Shiv cards, with Blade Dance being the best example, but does not need to run shivs to be powerful. Strangely enough, this works quite well with Wraith form since it prevents the tiny amount of incoming damage without forcing you to commit to block cards. Note that X cost cards can be played with 0 energy just to trigger this effect. Be aware that dexterity does not increase the block amount, nor is it reduced by frail. This is a brilliant power for the Heart fight - Beat of Death deals damage every time you play a card, and After Image completely offsets that. Higher ascension has more Beat of Death damage, and the Heart can buff this damage too. On the other hand, 3+ after images make the passive virtually non-existent.

name: Alchemize
description: Obtain a random potion. Exhaust.
descriptionplus: Obtain a random potion. Exhaust.
statement: Alchemize is a unique and powerful skill that I would rarely skip but often loses out to better alternatives, particularly rare cards. This card has considerable synergy with Burst. At higher ascensions, you're only offered two potion slots unless you take Potion Belt which means you don't get to store up a great amount of potions for important elite or boss battles. Obviously, never take this if you have Sozu. On the other hand, Toy Ornithopter means consistent healing which is important to the Silent.  If I find I have a lot of energy, I take this card as I know I can afford to play it without taking too many risks, since the potion that you get is always random.

name: All-Out Attack
description: Deal ^10 damage to ALL enemies. Discard 1 card at random.
descriptionplus: Deal ^14 damage to ALL enemies. Discard 1 card at random.
statement: All-out attack is an okay card and can be strong enough in act one to make up for the fact that it becomes worse and worse throughout the run. The fact that it discards a random card isn't always possible to play around, as sometimes you need to start a turn with all-out attack before playing the rest of your turn. Even though it has discard synergy, it doesn't really fit in a discard deck as you are unable to guarantee which card it will discard.

name: Backflip
description: Gain ^5 Block. Draw 2 cards.
descriptionplus: Gain ^8 Block. Draw 2 cards.
statement: Backflip is part of the Silent’s bread and butter. It is very common to finish a run with 2 copies of this. Although it is powerful later on, I would not always recommend picking up a backflip in act 1 unless you have some other source of energy gain or enough 0 cost cards to make the draw worth it.

name: Backstab
description: Innate. Deal ^11 damage. Exhaust.
descriptionplus: Innate Deal ^15 damage. Exhaust.
statement: Backstab is a brilliant proactive card that can finish an enemy on turn 1 which is extremely valuable. The fact that it is innate is both an upside and a drawback: on the one hand, it's guaranteed damage on turn 1, but on the other hand it is one less source of block on your opening turn. If you don't have your starting relic, it can sometimes be impossible to spend all of your energy on turn 1. I would always pick one copy of this, potentially take two, but normally taking three is pushing your luck.

name: Bane
description: Deal ^7 damage. If the enemy is Poisoned, deal ^7 damage again.
descriptionplus: Deal ^10 damage. If the enemy is Poisoned, deal ^10 damage again.
statement: If you have at least one or two sources of poison in your deck, this card is usually worth it. It's a decent amount of damage for 1 energy, and scales fairly well with strength. It is in a strange place, because typically if you are running a deck that focuses on poison you don't need want or big attacks. Nonetheless, this works very reliably with cards like crippling cloud and noxious fumes.

name: Blade Dance
description: Add ^3 Shivs to your hand.
descriptionplus: Add ^4 Shivs to your hand.
statement: Blade Dance is obviously very important to shiv decks, but on top of this it also synergises very well with certain relics. Kunai and Shuriken are perhaps the two most notable ones (always upgrade quickly if you have these), but relics like Ink Bottle, Pen Nib, and any others that trigger after a certain number of cards or attacks have been played also have great synergies with this. Be aware of the time eater and the heart.

name: Blur
description: Gain ^5 Block. Block is not removed at the start of your next turn.
descriptionplus: Gain ^8 Block. Block is not removed at the start of your next turn.
statement: Blur has a lot of potential, and even in the worst case scenario is 5 block for this turn and next turn. It allows the Silent to block in advance of a massive attack, or make use of a hand of all defends even on turns when she is not being attacked. Some cards such as after image allow the Silent to generate block even without trying to, and this card can help preserve some of this block. I sometimes take one or two Blurs from act one to act 2, and in theory having enough Blurs in your deck can cause you to never lose any block again. In practice, however, a deck with that much defend is not proactive enough to win.

name: Bouncing Flask
description: Apply 3 Poison to a random enemy ^3 times.
descriptionplus: Apply 3 Poison to a random enemy ^4 times.
statement: Bouncing flask is an important card in poison decks. Against single target enemies, the randomness of this card is fully negated. Since it is poison, it works well against targets with high health totals such as elites or bosses. The fact that it includes three or four applications of poison means that it is very useful for burning through multiple stacks of Artifact, for example against the Bronze Automaton. The fact that the targets are random makes this slightly more awkward in hallway fights, where it is difficult to guarantee where the poison will go. Sometimes, if this is in your opening hand, you should play it out first and then decide which targets to kill first based on where it landed.

name: Bullet Time
description: You cannot draw any cards this turn. Reduce the cost of cards in your hand to 0 this turn.
descriptionplus: You cannot draw any cards this turn. Reduce the cost of cards in your hand to 0 this turn.
statement: Bullet time is a difficult card to make the most out of. The silent typically runs a decent amount of cheap cards anyway, which makes the discount from this card negligible in most cases. It is best to draw before playing bullet time which means you normally need additional energy to be able to pull this off. If you find that you are consistently drawing a lot and ending the turn with big hands, feel free to put one in your deck, but most of the time bullet time ends up dead in my hand. Obviously, if your deck is leaning towards more expensive cards such as Wraith form and Nightmare this card will work a lot better. Since the Silent has so many strong rare cards, Bullet Time usually loses out.

name: Burst
description: This turn your next ^Skill is played twice.
descriptionplus: This turn your next ^2 Skills are played twice.
statement: Burst is a relatively strong card that greatly depends on your deck. The worst case scenario for this card is that you draw it on a turn where you have no other skills. On the other hand, if you can burst a key card skill as Malaise, Catalyst, or Adrenaline it becomes incredibly valuable. Due to its inconsistency, I often find myself picking other rares over burst but that is not to say that it can't be game winning in specific decks. Also note that this works with relics such as letter opener due to the increased number of skills being played.

name: Calculated Gamble
description: Discard your hand, then draw that many cards. ^Exhaust.
descriptionplus: Discard your hand, then draw that many cards.
statement: Ironically, calculated gamble is usually a safe bet in the early game. It is a way to redraw your hand for free with the only downside of drawing one less card. It synergises incredibly well with discard relics such as tingsha and tough bandages without forcing you into the archetype. In a full discard deck that involves infinitely cycling with Tactician, Multiple upgraded copies of calculated gamble are almost essential.

name: Caltrops
description: Whenever you are attacked, deal ^3 damage to the attacker.
descriptionplus: Whenever you are attacked, deal ^5 damage to the attacker.
statement: Caltrops can work well in silence due to her ability to stack up absurd amounts of block. Although this won't when encounters on its own, it is particularly powerful versus Hexaghost, the heart, and annihilates the birds. For this reason I would consider picking one up in act one especially if I know I will be fighting Hexaghost. Beyond this point, any additional copies of caltrops should only be considered for their dps against the heart.

name: Catalyst
description: ^Double an enemy's Poison. Exhaust.
descriptionplus: ^Triple an enemy's Poison. Exhaust.
statement: Catalyst is perhaps the single highest damage card the silent has access to. Although it requires some setup, it can turn boss encounters into an absolute joke. Be wary of bosses who can remove their debuffs, such as the champ and the time eater, because otherwise you will have to begin stacking poison all over again. Having 2 copies of catalyst makes it much more consistent, as sometimes you draw the first copy too early before there is significant poison on the target, and sometimes when you are cycling through the deck for the second time you might find that you are waiting on it for too long. Also, the difference between three times as much poison and nine times as much poison is extremely significant. Catalyst is a brilliant target for nightmare for this reason. Make sure not to pull the trigger too early on this card, as tripling five damage is considerably worse than tripling 20 damage.

name: Choke
description: Deal 12 damage. Whenever you play a card this turn, targeted enemy loses ^3 HP.
descriptionplus: Deal 12 damage. Whenever you play a card this turn, targeted enemy loses ^5 HP.
statement: Choke is often an unwieldy card. Its high energy cost makes it difficult to follow up with additional cards. Its most obvious synergy is shiv decks that are able to play a lot of cards on the same turn. However, I find that I most often take it when running an infinite discard deck enabled by tactician, as even without Tingsha this gives the deck a constant source of damage while it tries to continuously cycle. Outside of these scenarios, Choke typically underperforms, so I would not normally recommend picking it.

name: Cloak And Dagger
description: Gain 6 Block. Add ^1 Shiv to your hand.
descriptionplus: Gain 6 Block. Add ^2 Shivs to your hand.
statement: Cloak and dagger is a consistently strong common card in the silent. It grants both a source of damage and defense and is easy to pick up. It is brilliant during act one. A deck does not need to be running the Shiv archetype to warrant picking this up. Note that it is very reliable at triggering Orange Pellets, as it is a skill and an attack for 1 energy.

name: Concentrate
description: Discard ^3 cards. Gain [energy] [energy].
descriptionplus: Discard ^2 cards. Gain [energy] [energy].
statement: Concentrate is very difficult to use efficiently due to the heavy number of cards that it discards. Unless you're running a deck which has a considerable amount of draw, it is usually impossible to spend all of the energy generated by the card. The one main exception for this rule is unceasing top, as even if you run out of cards you will continue to draw some until you run out of energy or hit a curse or status card. Ice Cream also works well with Concentrate. Take with caution.

name: Corpse Explosion
description: Apply ^6 Poison&#46 When an enemy dies, deal damage equal to its MAX HP to ALL enemies.
descriptionplus: Apply ^9 Poison&#46 When an enemy dies, deal damage equal to its MAX HP to ALL enemies.
statement: Corpse explosion is a brilliant and unique card that can singlehandedly destroy corridor fights. It is also extremely good versus Deca and Donu. Be aware that corpse explosion goes through two artifact stacks - the first one is the poison, and the 2nd is the explosive effect. In fights you would normally attack the enemy with the lowest health to kill it as soon as possible - when playing with corpse explosion, keep in mind how the splash damage will affect the rest of the enemies. Even in decks that don't rely on poison, this card is very reliable.

name: Crippling Cloud
description: Apply ^4 Poison and 2 Weak to ALL enemies. Exhaust.
descriptionplus: Apply ^7 Poison and 2 Weak to ALL enemies. Exhaust.
statement: Crippling cloud is the silent equivalent of shockwave. If drawn early, it is a reliable aoe debuff with some defense thrown in. This card works particularly well with sadistic nature if you are able to pull it beforehand. A decent standalone card.

name: Dagger Spray
description: Deal ^4 damage to ALL enemies twice.
descriptionplus: Deal ^6 damage to ALL enemies twice.
statement: Dagger spray is a very solid, reliable source of damage for the Silent. It scales well with strength and is great at clearing trash mobs on act 1. It can also be useful for killing the birds at the start of act 2. After act 1, I would only consider taking this card if you are lacking aoe damage or have some specific synergies that work with dagger spray, for example Envenom.

name: Dagger Throw
description: Deal ^9 damage. Draw 1 card. Discard 1 card.
descriptionplus: Deal ^12 damage. Draw 1 card. Discard 1 card.
statement: Dagger Throw is a great proactive card to take for act one when the silent is lacking in damage. It is particularly strong versus the gremlin nob.  The discard effect of this card is negligible, since the card that you are discarding you would not normally have the energy to play anyway, and even once you have acquired enough energy relics you're only discarding the worst card in your hand anyway. If you do end up with relics that benefit from discard, you can segue into a discard heavy deck very easily, but this card does not force you to commit to the archetype.

name: Dash
description: Gain ^10 Block. Deal ^10 damage.
descriptionplus: Gain ^13 Block. Deal ^13 damage.
statement: Dash, like iron wave, is a decent pick in act one because it is so strong versus the gremlin nob. Also, due to its large numbers, it is not as greatly affected by lagavulin’s debuff. Again, it benefits from strength and dexterity but not quite as efficiently as iron wave does. I would be happy to pick one or two of these up over the course of my run.

name: Deadly Poison
description: Apply ^5 Poison.
descriptionplus: Apply ^7 Poison.
statement: Deadly poison is a basic and simple poison card for the silent. I try to pick one of these up in act one just in case I fight lagavulin as the strength debuff does not affect poison. It can also be okay versus the birds as its damage is not reduced by flight. Additionally, poison gets its maximum value versus bosses usually, So if you find that your deck does not have much damage in the early game picking one up can help you beat the act one boss. Any deck that is going down the poison archetype should pick this up.

name: Deflect
description: Gain ^4 Block.
descriptionplus: Gain ^7 Block.
statement: Although it may look like deflect doesn't have any downsides, if you find that you are not able to spend all of your energy in a turn then you have used it inefficiently. A 0 cost card is fine in act one but becomes worse as the game progresses. The four block is nothing to write home about that can negate some damage against the first few mobs. This is obviously a bad card versus the time eater and the heart. For this reason, I would rarely pick this.

name: Die Die Die
description: Deal ^13 damage to ALL enemies. Exhaust.
descriptionplus: Deal ^17 damage to ALL enemies. Exhaust.
statement: Die die die is a solid card that grants the silent some frontloaded aoe damage which she is sometimes lacking in. Although this card looks significantly better than dagger spray, which is its nearest equivalent, it does not benefit from strength in the same way and also it exhausts, making it considerably worse. Since the silent has so many powerful rares, die die die rarely wins out. however, if it is offered next to other cards that are not worth taking, feel free to pick it up.

name: Distraction
description: Add a random Skill to your hand. It costs 0 this turn. Exhaust.
descriptionplus: Add a random Skill to your hand. It costs 0 this turn. Exhaust.
statement: The main downside of distraction is its randomness. For example, it could create a deflect which would be terrible value for this card. Although this situation is unlikely to occur, I feel it is important to control as much RNG in the game as possible, which is why I rarely pick this. Obviously, if it produces a high cost card it can have good value. This card synergises particularly well with letter opener, as it provides two instantly playable skills for 1 or 0 energy.

name: Dodge and Roll
description: Gain ^4 Block. Next turn gain ^4 Block.
descriptionplus: Gain ^6 Block. Next turn gain ^6 Block.
statement: Dodge and roll is a very solid basic card in the silent. Many silent decks rely on being able to block for high amounts, and since this block is spread over two turns it is very rare that it would get no value (unlike drawing a defend on a turn where no monsters are attacking). the biggest consideration for this card is that dexterity it applied to this twice, as it affects both turns that it blocks on. This makes it pair extremely well with dexterity effects, and if your deck has any sources of dexterity I would be happy to pick up multiple copies of this card.

name: Doppelganger
description: Next turn, draw ^X cards and gain ^X Energy.
descriptionplus: Next turn, draw ^X+1 cards and gain ^X+1 Energy.
statement: Doppelganger is a way to make use of turns where you have dead hands. My main issue with it is that you should not be aiming to build a deck that has dead hands in the 1st place. It also contributes to the problem of giving you a dead hand, as the card does nothing on its own. I think the best use of this card is upgrading it and playing it for zero energy as a way to draw one card and gain one energy at the cost of one card in your hand this turn. strangely enough, it can synergise well with flechettes, as the additional draws allow you to have a big hand which likely has a lot of skills in. Burst allows you to play this card twice which can be good value, but this card mostly only synergises with Chemical X for obvious reasons. If you have Chemical X I would strongly consider taking this card.

name: Endless Agony
description: Whenever you draw this card, add a copy of it to your hand. Deal ^4 damage. Exhaust.
descriptionplus: Whenever you draw this card, add a copy of it to your hand. Deal ^6 damage. Exhaust.
statement: Endless agony is an odd card. The text that allows you to continuously create multiple copies in your deck tends to be completely irrelevant, as fights are either over before you draw your next couple of copies, or because you don't actually want to draw another copy of endless agony. Frontloaded damage is typically very important in this game in order to defeat a single target early on. Delaying damage is rarely recommended. If we consider this as a card to simply be played when drawn, this card can have considerable synergy with dead branch, which allows you to deal 8 damage and create 2 new cards in your hand at the same time. this is usually a good thing, although dead branch is renowned for clogging up your deck with cards you didn't want.

name: Envenom
description: Whenever an attack deals unblocked damage, apply 1 Poison.
descriptionplus: Whenever an attack deals unblocked damage, apply 1 Poison.
statement: The main problem with envenom is its high energy cost. It is a very slow acting source of damage and thus sometimes useless in hallway fights. It is a solid rare, although I typically find that other silent prayers are more powerful. Obviously, envenom synergises fairly well with shiv decks and extremely well with Snecko Skull, essentially doubling the amount of poison it applies. Due to it being a hybrid of a shiv deck and a poison deck, it is fairly niche in its use; on the other hand, it is not difficult to use even if the synergy is not at an extremely high power level.

name: Escape Plan
description: Draw 1 card. If the card is a Skill, gain ^3 Block.
descriptionplus: Draw 1 card. If the card is a Skill, gain ^5 Block.
statement: Escape plan looks like a great deal: it is a card that cycles itself for free with a potential upside. The only problem with this is: the gremlin nob, the time eater, the chosen, and the heart. all of these enemies make escape plan considerably worse. If you are not worried about these enemies then feel free to take as many copies of escape plan as you like, but be aware that at ascension 20 there is a 67% chance that you will face the time eater.

name: Eviscerate
description: Costs 1 less Energy for each card discarded this turn. Deal ^7 damage three times.
descriptionplus: Costs 1 less Energy for each card discarded this turn. Deal ^9 damage three times.
statement: I almost never pick eviscerate, as the conditions for making the card cheaper are very difficult to pull off. If you use a card to discard 2 cards, you now have 2 cards in hand one of which is eviscerate and have done nothing else. Ironically, discarding usually means that you float energy because you no longer have other cards to spend energy on. The best solution to this problem is drafting an acrobatics. Even at 2 energy, this card is not especially good, and only above average value when it reaches 1 energy or less, which can be difficult to pull off. Tools of the trade can help you manage this, and well laid plans allows you to have synergistic cards in hand at the same time. Note that eviscerate benefits greatly from strength, as one point of strength is equal to three points of damage.

name: Expertise
description: Draw cards until you have ^6 in hand.
descriptionplus: Draw cards until you have ^7 in hand.
statement: Expertise is a somewhat niche card that I rarely draft. If you have a deck that consistently has five or six energy at the start of its turns comment I would recommend taking it as it is a very inexpensive way to refill your hand after having played out a lot of cards. It does not work in the same way as calculated gamble which is used to reshuffle a bad hand. Because it requires so much energy to be useful, I definitely would not pick this up in act one and possibly not act two either. It is a decent card to pick in infinite cycle discard decks due to it being a very cheap way to refill your hand once you start to run out of cards.

name: Finisher
description: Deal ^6 damage for each Attack played this turn.
descriptionplus: Deal ^8 damage for each Attack played this turn.
statement: Finisher is an obvious choice in shiv decks. It synergises well with strength, like shiv decks do. Once you have four or more energy per turn, it is much easier to set up a big finisher turn – otherwise, it is doing about 12 damage at most. This card works particularly well with Runic Pyramid, as you are able to ensure that you have the hand you need to set up a huge attack. The worst case scenario is drawing this card with no other attacks which is usually quite rare.

name: Flechettes
description: Deal ^4 damage for each Skill in your hand.
descriptionplus: Deal ^6 damage for each Skill in your hand.
statement: The silent has some very powerful skills and as such Flechettes can get a surprising amount of value. It scales very well with strength comma and works exceptionally well withdraw cards such as backflip and acrobatics. Since it does not require you to actually play the skills, It can be effective even with low energy. It is fairly inconsistent, just like finisher, but can be incredibly energy efficient in the right circumstances.

name: Flying Knee
description: Deal ^8 damage. Next turn gain [energy].
descriptionplus: Deal ^11 damage. Next turn gain [energy].
statement: Although flying knee is a fairly unremarkable card, it usually performs rather well. The energy is almost always relevant and although having an energy relic is much better, it can help carry later acts in runs where you don't find the energy relics that you want. The damage is decent but i wouldn't upgrade this card in a hurry.

name: Footwork
description: Gain ^2 Dexterity.
descriptionplus: Gain ^3 Dexterity.
statement: Footwork is a very solid and consistent tool for the silent. It allows her to negate enormous amounts of damage using just basic defend cards. The more footworks you have the better. It won't win you the game on its own but is almost never bad.

name: Glass Knife
description: Deal ^8 damage twice. Glass Knife's damage is lowered by 2 this combat.
descriptionplus: Deal ^12 damage twice. Glass Knife's damage is lowered by 2 this combat.
statement: Glass knife is a very solid source of damage for hallway fights. Its up-front damage is extremely energy efficient and can sometimes help kill an enemy on turn one. Due to the fact that the damage eventually drops off, this card is not as strong in elites and especially in boss fights. This card should be considered an upgrade priority. Obviously, the bigger your deck is the less noticeable the reduction effect is. I would pick this card over passing, but some of the silent’s rare cards are better win conditions.

name: Grand Finale
description: Can only be played if there are no cards in your draw pile. Deal ^50 damage to ALL enemies.
descriptionplus: Can only be played if there are no cards in your draw pile. Deal ^60 damage to ALL enemies.
statement: Grand finale is an extremely difficult card to pull off. I would only ever consider using this in a real deck if I were offered it within the first 3 fights of the game. It requires an extremely small deck to make sure that this card can be consistently played over multiple turns. Even if you are able to play grand finale every time you shuffle your deck, in a 20 card deck that might still be every three or four turns which is not fast enough. To make this card work, it is important to consider your draw amounts - for example, Backflip draws 2 cards whereas Quick Slash draws 1. By having a variety of draw amounts in your deck if you can ensure that you can always empty your draw pile without overdrawing. It is possible to run this card as your only source of damage and I would recommend that. Once you get to a very slim deck, it is easy to play this card two or three times in a single turn which is enough to dispatch most foes. Do not take this card unless you intend to build your deck around it. Another honorable mention is Well laid plans which ensures that this card stays in your hand until it is playable, which is useful in 12-20 card decks. However, for this strategy to work your deck should already be small enough to play it multiple times over without the need for retaining.

name: Heel Hook
description: Deal ^5 damage. If the enemy has Weak, Gain [energy] and draw 1 card.
descriptionplus: Deal ^8 damage. If the enemy has Weak, Gain [energy] and draw 1 card.
statement: In my opinion, heel hook is a bit of a noob trap. Although the free value is extremely tempting, at best this card is a free five damage which is negligible in the long run. With enough heel hooks it is possible to create a near-infinite cycle deck but this strategy is extremely unreliable as you can never be sure how many copies you will find, and the bigger your deck gets the sparser your sources of weak become. It might help for act 1 if your Neutralize is upgraded early but in most scenarios I would recommend passing since it's very often worse than strike.

name: Infinite Blades
description: At the start of your turn, add a Shiv to your hand.
descriptionplus: ^Innate. At the start of your turn, add a Shiv to your hand.
statement: Infinite blades is a free four damage every turn for one energy. If you are approaching an act 1 boss and feel like you do not have enough dps to take it down, feel free to pick this up. It does not rely on shiv synergies, such as accuracy, but it does work considerably well with them. A solid and reliable card.

name: Leg Sweep
description: Apply ^2 Weak. Gain ^11 Block.
descriptionplus: Apply ^3 Weak. Gain ^14 Block.
statement: Leg sweep is one of the silent’s most reliable sources of damage negation. It is fairly easy to find since it is only uncommon rarity, blocks for a decent amount and also applies weak for subsequent turns. Having two to three of these in your deck is usually a good thing.

name: Malaise
description: Enemy loses X Strength&#46 Apply X Weak. Exhaust.
descriptionplus: Enemy loses ^X+1 Strength&#46 Apply ^X+1 Weak. Exhaust.
statement: Malaise is a very powerful card, and in some cases can render fights laughable. With enough energy certain enemies are no longer able to deal damage anymore. The Hexaghost, byrds, three-headed plants, the Time-Eater, Deca and Donu, the Awakened and the Heart can all be made much easier with a well-timed Malaise. Works best with a lot of energy.

name: Masterful Stab
description: Cost 1 additional [energy] for each time you lose HP this combat. Deal ^12 Damage.
descriptionplus: Cost 1 additional [energy] for each time you lose HP this combat. Deal ^16 Damage.
statement: Masterful stab is an extremely energy efficient card if you have not taken any damage. Since the silent does not have any healing effects in her class, it is surprisingly common to take 0 damage in a fight. Even after having taken damage once, this card is still worth playing for one energy. If a fight goes for long enough this can become a five cost curse in your deck but in most hallway fights that is not an important factor. In that sense, it is quite similar to glass knife in that it is bad in long fights and good in short ones.

name: Neutralize
description: Deal ^3 damage. Apply ^1 Weak.
descriptionplus: Deal ^4 damage. Apply ^2 Weak.
statement: Neutralize is a brilliant starter card for the silent. It is very often the first card that I choose to upgrade because of its weaken effect. I would never choose to get rid of this card (unless running a very specific archetype that requires tiny deck).

name: Nightmare
description: Choose a card. Next turn, add 3 copies of that card into your hand. Exhaust.
descriptionplus: Choose a card. Next turn, add 3 copies of that card into your hand. Exhaust.
statement: Although nightmare might look unremarkable, this card can be completely game winning in the right scenario. For example, if you cast Nightmare on an upgraded catalyst, you can triple something’s poison 4 times (x81 poison). Well-laid Plans is a must-have if you are taking nightmare in order to retain either the card to be copied or nightmare itself. This card often requires a lot of energy because it is difficult to play this without taking damage. For this reason I would also recommend upgrading it. It tends to be more useful in boss fights when you are able to copy an important power or skill.

name: Noxious Fumes
description: At the start of your turn, apply 2 Poison to ALL enemies.
descriptionplus: At the start of your turn, apply ^3 Poison to ALL enemies.
statement: Noxious fumes is always a great pick in any silent deck. Even when you are not running a poison death, it is a slow but reliable way to whittle down high health enemies over multiple turns for just one energy. It is also exceptionally good at burning away stacks of artifact very cheaply which can be relevant versus Deca and Donu and also the Heart. Of all of the poison cards in the game, this is the one I would most want to pick if I was not fully investing in a poison deck. Obviously this also works very well in poison decks too. Having one or two noxious fumes in your deck is never a bad idea.

name: Outmaneuver
description: Next turn gain [energy] [energy].
descriptionplus: Next turn gain [energy] [energy] [energy].
statement: Outmaneuver is a difficult and awkward card to use. It allows you 2 make the most of a dead hand by pushing the NRG to your next turn, but in most scenarios you don't want to have a dead hand in the 1st place and this card contributes to that. There is no guarantee that the NRG will be useful on the next turn because it is usually impossible to know which cards you will be drawing. For this reason, I very rarely pick this card. Even a flying knee seems better. The best case scenario makes use of well laid plans in addition to X cost cards, such as Malaise.

name: Phantasmal Killer
description: On your next turn, your Attack damage is doubled.
descriptionplus: On your next turn, your Attack damage is doubled.
statement: Phantasmal killer is an extremely niche card. It is fairly rare that the silent runs a heavy damage deck with strength outside of shiv decks, but in cases where she does this card can be completely devastating. It allows your glass knife to do 48 damage for one energy, for example. The difficulty lies in being able to play the card without being punished too hard (which is why I would recommend upgrading this card) and also being able to set up your next turn to have lots of attacks. it has very well with well laid plans which allows you to retain 2 hard hitting attacks that you will guaranteed be able to play when you have double damage.

name: Piercing Wail
description: ALL enemies lose ^6 Strength for 1 turn. Exhaust.
descriptionplus: ALL enemies lose ^8 Strength for 1 turn. Exhaust.
statement: Piercing Wail is one of the best common cards that the silent has. Although it might not look better than a simple defend, it affects multiple enemies and is even more effective versus multihit attacks (such as the Dagger Elite from Act 2 or the Heart’s 15-hit attack). Its only downside is that it exhausts, but to counteract this I would be happy to pick up two 3 copies of this card in my deck. Since the card is common, this is fairly easy to do. It is negated by artifact, but the simple fact that this card burns one artifact off each enemy for one energy means it is usually still worth it. Note that strength reduction is also more effective than block when you are vulnerable or frail.

name: Poisoned Stab
description: Deal ^6 damage. Apply ^3 Poison.
descriptionplus: Deal ^8 damage. Apply ^4 Poison.
statement: Poisoned stab is a decent but unremarkable card that I normally only pick up in act one, especially if I have no other source of poison. The increased DPS can be valuable against enemies with high health totals such as the act one bosses and the poison is still effective versus lagavulin despite the strength reduction debuff. It is not the backbone of any poison deck archetype but can be useful for burning artifact stacks, particularly against the spherical sentry who is very susceptible to poison.

name: Predator
description: Deal ^15 damage. Next turn, draw 2 additional cards.
descriptionplus: Deal ^20 damage. Next turn, draw 2 additional cards.
statement: Predator is a high damage mid cost attack for the silent that comes with some utility that might seem more fitting for the ironclad. Although it is fairly expensive which is uncommon for the silent, predator is actually extremely affective versus The Gremlin Nob and Lagavulin. The gremlin nob requires you to draw more cards in order to be able to make the most of your energy on every turn and this card allows you to do this whilst playing an attack. Lagavulin on the other hand reduces your strength which can render your strikes completely ineffective after nine turns. However due to the high damage total of the predator cards they are still able to do around 8 or 9 damage at this point. Predator pairs well with zero cost cards such as neutralise or slice as early on you are not going to be able to play all of the 7 cards that you will draw on the turn after this card is played.

name: Prepared
description: Draw ^1 card. Discard ^1 card.
descriptionplus: Draw ^2 cards. Discard ^2 cards.
statement: Prepared is fairly effective in discard decks, and can be useful if you somehow end up with a deck that has a lot of curses in. Note that there is a net loss in card advantage when playing this card , as although it replaces one card in your hand comma the card itself must be played as well. This is why it is impossible to generate an infinite discard deck through just prepared alone. All in all, this card is not particularly effective versus the chosen comma the time eater, and the heart, which is why at high ascension I typically pass over picking this card.

name: Quick Slash
description: Deal ^8 damage. Draw 1 card.
descriptionplus: Deal ^12 damage. Draw 1 card.
statement: Quick slash is an alright card for act 1, or an OK source of draw heading into act 2 and 3 if you have managed to pick up some energy relics but not been able to draft strong draw effects such as backflip or acrobatics. Unfortunately, its upgrade only increases its damage and not its draw amount, which is why I would be very hesitant to upgrade this card.

name: Reflex
description: Unplayable. If this card is discarded from your hand, draw ^2 cards.
descriptionplus: Unplayable. If this card is discarded from your hand, draw ^3 cards.
