statement: Reflex is one of the cards that allows the infinite discard deck to work. It is not as impressive as tactician, but on the other hand is less rare. Picking this without at least three discard effects is usually a recipe for disaster, as this card becomes a curse in your deck most of the time. Obviously, this card works exceptionally well with tools of the trade which is strong enough on its own.

name: Riddle with Holes
description: Deal ^3 damage 5 times.
descriptionplus: Deal ^4 damage 5 times.
statement: Riddle with holes is a fairly expensive attack for the silent. I usually would not consider drafting it unless I somehow had some source of strength, which is rare for the silent. However, some relics such as girya and vajra fit the bill. 20 damage for a 2 cost card is not that impressive, but 25 to 30 is very cost efficient. If you are offered the JAX event in act 2, this works very well with riddled with holes. unsurprisingly, this card pairs very well with envenom, as it also applies five stacks of poison.

name: Setup
description: Place a card in your hand on top of your draw pile. It cost 0 until it is played.
descriptionplus: Place a card in your hand on top of your draw pile. It cost 0 until it is played.
statement: Set up is a very difficult card to get any value out of. Not only do you have to draw an expensive card on the same turn as this card, you also are using two of the five cards that you get this turn to do nothing. It also doesn't have any benefit until the discounted card has been played. This is much too slow for higher ascensions and at best saves you 3 energy. If you draw set up, a good set up target comma and draw all on the same turn you can make use of the discount immediately. However this is extremely unlikely to happen and generally isn't worth it. The silent also does not have any 4 cost or 5 cost cards that could abuse this mechanic.

name: Skewer
description: Deal ^7 damage X times.
descriptionplus: Deal ^10 damage X times.
statement: Skewer is a versatile and effective card for the silent. Whenever you draw an ex cost card you can guarantee that you will get maximum use of your energy this turn. This makes it exceptionally good versus the gremlin nob and the sentries in act one where your hands can be awkward. it has acceptable damage which scales well with strength, and X cost cards can be played for zero energy whilst still triggering relic effects such as kunai or shuriken.

name: Slice
description: Deal ^6 damage.
descriptionplus: Deal ^9 damage.
statement: Slice is an acceptable pick for act one when you are normally unable to play your entire hand because you do not have enough energy. After act one when you begin picking up energy relics, this card becomes considerably worse. It is worth mentioning that it does work with wrist blade and can therefore complement shiv decks in certain scenarios.

name: Sneaky Strike
description: Deal ^12 damage. If you have discarded a card this turn, gain [energy] [energy].
descriptionplus: Deal ^16 damage. If you have discarded a card this turn, gain [energy] [energy].
statement: Being able to deal 12 damage for zero energy is very tempting. It is however fairly difficult to ensure that you can play your one energy discard effect before playing this card in order to trigger the energy refund in the correct order. If you are playing a discard deck or have three or more discard cards in your deck anyway, this card can become fairly reliable, however its upside is fairly negligible for its difficult to set up. Note that tools of the trade and well laid plans allow you to always benefit from the discounted cost.

name: Storm of Steel
description: Discard your hand. Add 1 ^ Shiv to your hand for each card discarded.
descriptionplus: Discard your hand. Add 1 ^Upgraded Shiv to your hand for each card discarded.
statement: Storm of steel is an interesting rare card. If paired with a strong draw effect, this can generate a lot of additional damage cheaply. It isn't always easy to set up these turns however. It obviously works exceptionally well with accuracy kunai and shuriken, but often I find that I am unable to use all of my energy efficiently while still hitting a decent amount of cards with storm of steel. I have had most success with this card when pairing it with dead branch, as you are not required to spend the rest of your energy playing cards before playing storm of steel, since the remaining one or two energy can be spent on cards that are generated from your shivs.

name: Sucker Punch
description: Deal ^7 damage. Apply ^1 Weak.
descriptionplus: Deal ^9 damage. Apply ^2 Weak.
statement: Sucker punch is a valuable source of weak in the silent. Weak is one of the silent’s main means of damage mitigation and this is a common card, making it easy to pick up early on in the run. Since you begin with the Neutralize, this ensures that you have a decent number of weak turns for the enemy when you have one or two sucker punches in your deck.

name: Survivor
description: Gain ^8 Block. Discard a card.
descriptionplus: Gain ^11 Block. Discard a card.
statement: Survivor is another very good starter card for the silent. Normally, the discard effect is negligible; in most scenarios you are able to play survivor as the very last card of the turn and if you have an empty hand you do not discard anything. The premium block value on this card due to its discard effect is therefore fairly irrelevant, and in some situations having the discard effect can actually be to your advantage.

name: Tactician
description: Unplayable. If this card is discarded from your hand, gain [energy].
descriptionplus: Unplayable. If this card is discarded from your hand, gain [energy] [energy].
statement: I would only pick tactician in decks that are investing heavily in the infinite discard archetype: in a small enough deck which runs acrobatics, calculated gamble, and has a Tingsha or Letter Opener, you can kill enemies in one turn. Note that it does work exceptionally well with tools of the trade and well laid plans can also help guarantee the effectiveness of this card.

name: Terror
description: Apply 99 Vulnerable. Exhaust.
descriptionplus: Apply 99 Vulnerable. Exhaust.
statement: When running a few powerful attacks on the silent, such as glass knife, dagger spray or die die die, terror can be a powerful card. It is usually fine to pick one up no matter what deck you're running as this silent will still have her basic strikes and some other sources of attack damage. The only time you would want to consider taking multiple copies of terror is versus the awakened and the time eater, as both of them have a way to remove the vulnerable debuff.

name: Tools of the Trade
description: At the start of your turn, draw 1 card and discard 1 card.
descriptionplus: At the start of your turn, draw 1 card and discard 1 card.
statement: Tools of the trade is a powerful and reliable power for the silent, although its effects are not usually game winning. Note that it also works exceptionally well with discard effects and cards that work by being discarded, such as a tactician and reflex. Even in decks that do not at all rely upon the discard effect, it can guarantee a decent hand and many times you are able to just discard a defend or strike or some card that is not relevant to this turn without any worry. This card obviously has incredible synergy with hovering kite.

name: Unload
description: Deal ^14 damage. Discard all non-Attack cards.
descriptionplus: Deal ^18 damage. Discard all non-Attack cards.
statement: Unload is an above average attack with a fairly negligible downside. It can usually be played last on a turn, meaning that the discard effect is irrelevant. the silent has much more powerful and game winning rares, meaning that I rarely pick this card up, but I would usually pick this card over passing. Note that this card has fairly considerable anti synergy with well laid plans, as discarding the skills and powers in your hand usually leaves you with nothing left to retain.

name: Well-Laid Plans
description: At the end of your turn, Retain up to ^1 card.
descriptionplus: At the end of your turn, Retain up to ^2 cards.
statement: Well laid plans is an exceptionally powerful card for the silent. When it used to cost 0 energy it was an instapick, exceptionally easy to play in fights for a considerable upside. Now that it costs 1 energy it is actually worth considering in a fight whether or not the one energy could be spent more effectively. in a longer boss fight or elite fight it is usually worth playing other power, but in a small hallway fight for example against the bandits, that one energy is typically better spent on an attack or a block. I would always be happy to pick up one or perhaps 2 copies of well laid plans in my deck, since sometimes one copy can find itself on the bottom of your deck and you need to make sure that you draw one early to be able to set up devastating turns with Catalyst, Grand Finale, Phantasmal Killer, Wraith Form, and Nightmare, just to name a few. In the worst case scenario, you are still able to hold an important block card for a dangerous turn, such as a Panic Button.

name: Wraith Form
description: Gain ^2 Intangible. At the end of your turn, lose 1 Dexterity.
descriptionplus: Gain ^3 Intangible. At the end of your turn, lose 1 Dexterity.
statement: Wraith Form is an extremely powerful card which has a very real downside. It is extremely effective in hallway fights where you do not expect to be fighting for a long time. When playing out boss fights, you typically don't want to play this card until you know that there are only three terms of combat left. Obviously it is impossible to know exactly when there are three turns of combat left but if you know the boss phases well enough you should be able to guess how long each flight will take you. Playing this card too rarely makes your defends do absolutely nothing and also really reduces the effectiveness of the rest of your blocks, and the silent will not last very long in these situations. The more wraith forms you have the better. If you are constantly intangible, whether or not you can block is completely irrelevant. A well timed nightmare can allow you to have 4 Wraith Forms in your deck with just one card. The other ways of negating the dexterity down effect are by having artifact ignore it or by using orange pellets, which cleanses the dexterity down over time and also cleanses any current negative dexterity stacks. Note that even when intangible you will still be taking chip damage which adds up overtime. For this reason some kind of plated armor effect such as thread and needle can really help you stay topped up.

description: Unplayable. While in hand, lose 1 HP when other cards are played.

name: Parasite
description: Unplayable. If transformed or removed from your deck, lose 3 Max HP.

name: Regret
description: Unplayable. At the end of your turn, lose 1 HP for each card in your hand.

name: Writhe
description: Unplayable. Innate.

name: Shame
description: Unplayable. At the end of your turn, gain 1 Frail.

name: Pride
description: Innate. At the end of your turn, place a copy of this card on top of your draw pile.

name: Curse of the Bell
description: Unplayable. Cannot be removed from your deck.

name: Aggregate
description: Gain [energy] for every ^4 cards in your draw pile.
descriptionplus: Gain [energy] for every ^3 cards in your draw pile.
statement: Aggregate is an unusually awkward card. Although it can provide 3-4 energy quite consistently, it solely depends on when it is drawn. If it is in the bottom 12 cards of the deck, it provides no benefit. As such your deck should be around 30 cards before you consider taking this. It synergises very well with bottled lightning as it can provide a lot of energy on turn one. Despite this, it is still sometimes difficult to use all of the energy that this card provides. For this reason, I rarely pick this card up. Cards that reshuffle your deck increase the consistency of this card.

name: All For One
description: Deal ^10 damage. Put all Cost 0 cards from your discard pile into your hand.
descriptionplus: Deal ^14 damage. Put all Cost 0 cards from your discard pile into your hand.
statement: All for one is one of the defect’s build-around archetypes. This class has an unusual amount of 0 cost cards, and being able to use all of those cards again in a single turn can be very effective. Unfortunately, if all for one is drawn early when your discard pile is quite low, sometimes you cannot pull any 0 cost cards. Hologram can help redraw All For One on a better turn. Claw is perhaps the best 0 cost card to benefit from all for one, as it can scale twice as quickly. However, claw is not necessary. It is worth considering upgrading Zap and Dualcast, since when these cards cost zero they can also be affected by all for one. Madness also has a unique interaction here.

name: Amplify
description: This turn, your next ^Power is played twice.
descriptionplus: This turn, your next ^2 ^Powers are played twice.
statement: Being able to double the effectiveness of a power is indeed very powerful. the reason this card is rated so lowly is because it is often difficult to draw amplify on the same turn as a tower. Amplify does not exhaust, and once your powers have all been played it becomes a dead draw. On the other hand, amplify synergises extremely well with creative AI since you are guaranteed to have a power in hand every single turn.

name: Auto-Shields
description: If you have 0 Block, gain ^11 Block.
descriptionplus: If you have 0 Block, gain ^15 Block.
statement: This card is a decent consideration for act one. It is very energy efficient and its downside is often negligible. The real problem with auto Shields is the increasing likelihood of picking up relics that provide incidental block at the start of a turn. Things like calipers, anchor, ornamental fan, and the abacus can prevent you from being able to get any block from this card. Furthermore, loop can trigger a Frost orb at the start of your turn and that two block completely negates also Shields.  Needless to say this card also has an anti synergy with itself. For this reason I would not normally pick up more than one copy.

name: Ball Lightning
description: Deal ^7 damage. Channel 1 Lightning.
descriptionplus: Deal ^11 damage. Channel 1 Lightning.
statement: Ball lightning is a decent pick up in act one as it allows you to fill your empty orb slots whilst doing damage. A lot of channel cards are skills which are not very effective versus the gremlin nob. that makes it particularly important if you are elite hunting in act one and it is still fine throughout later acts. It might be worth picking up multiple copies of ball lightning if you are running electrodynamics.

name: Barrage
description: Deal ^4 damage for each Channeled Orb.
descriptionplus: Deal ^6 damage for each Channeled Orb.
statement: Although barrage has a condition, it has the potential to greatly exceed the amount of damage you should be able to do with 1 energy. This card can do up to 60 damage. It also scales extremely well with strength. Early on this card is quite unimpressive due to a lack of orb slots and channel effects, but on longer fights and in later acts it is one of the defect’s heavier hitting cards.

name: Beam Cell
description: Deal ^3 damage and apply ^1 Vulnerable.
descriptionplus: Deal ^4 damage and apply ^2 Vulnerable.
statement: Although beam cell is an unremarkable card, it is one of the only sources of vulnerable in this class. If you have a deck that deals significant attack damage, definitely consider picking one or two copies up. It obviously synergises with all for one too.

name: Biased Cognition
description: Gain ^4 Focus. At the start of each turn, lose 1 Focus.
descriptionplus: Gain ^5 Focus. At the start of each turn, lose 1 Focus.
statement: Biased cognition is single-handedly the most powerful defect card for hallway fights. It is extremely fast acting, cheap, and has no downsides until turn 5. It is comparable to Wraith Form: you do not want to play this until you are sure that combat will be over before its effect wears off. This makes it a bit of a gamble in boss fights, but its benefits greatly outweigh its downsides. I would always recommend picking up at least one copy of this card. If you have any ways of getting artifact, the downside of this card can be fully negated making it incredibly powerful. Furthermore, orange pellets can remove the focus down debuff, and since this power is so cheap it is very easy to consistently pull this off on the turn that it is played.

name: Blizzard
description: Deal damage equal to ^2 times the Frost Channeled this combat to ALL enemies.
descriptionplus: Deal damage equal to ^3 times the Frost Channeled this combat to ALL enemies.
statement: More often than not, Blizzard is a pipe dream. Frost cards are few and far between, and the damage is very poor even after two cycles of your deck. Blizzard is simply too slow to be effective, and often the aoe aspect is completely irrelevant as there are rarely multiple enemies alive after one or two cycles of your deck. It can work as a sole source of damage in a very thin and Frost heavy deck, simply generating block until this does enough damage to kill. However, there are much more reliable sources of damage that are faster and require less set up. Even when picked up as early as floor one there is no guarantee that you will pick up enough Frost cards to support it (and obviously it is terrible early). Hologram can help you pull more Frost cards, or when you have stacked up enough allows you to play your Blizzard more frequently.

name: Boot Sequence
description: Gain ^10 Block. Innate. Exhaust.
descriptionplus: Gain ^13 Block. Innate. Exhaust.
statement: Boot sequence is a god-send. Turn one is frequently the most important turn of combat and being able to negate 10/13 damage for free is incredibly powerful. If you are not being attacked on turn 1, it is fine to let this card simply cycle back around for a later turn.

name: Buffer
description: Prevent the next ^time you would lose HP.
descriptionplus: Prevent the next ^2 ^times you would lose HP.
statement: Buffer can be a powerful card depending on the circumstances. Obviously, enemies such as the birds make this extremely ineffective. On the other hand, it could block a huge hit from the gremlin nob, the giant slime, or the heart. When picked, buffer should be a priority upgrade.

name: Capacitor
description: Gain ^2 Orb slots.
descriptionplus: Gain ^3 Orb slots.
statement: Capacitor is a very solid and consistent form of slot game in the defect. It is inexpensive, easy to play, and fits into every defect deck. It's upside is not present until you have channeled enough orbs, so make sure to bring channel cards with this. Note that the defect is only able to have 10 orb slots max, so typically two upgraded capacitors is sufficient.

name: Chaos
description: Channel ^1 random Orb.
descriptionplus: Channel ^2 random Orbs.
statement: Due to the unpredictable nature of chaos, I typically skip this card. When upgraded it can be a cheap way of quickly filling orb slots, especially in a deck with few channelling effects. The hidden power of chaos lies in its ability to cheaply generate plasma orbs. However, a 25% success chance for a card is not good enough, And more often than not you will get orbs that you did not want.

name: Chill
description: Channel 1 Frost for each enemy in combat. Exhaust.
descriptionplus: ^Innate. Channel 1 Frost for each enemy in combat. Exhaust.
statement: Chill is one of my favourite defect cards. It is incredibly energy efficient and is even higher value when you are able to upgrade it. This guarantees that chill affects every single enemy on the battlefield before any of them die. At its worst, it is still 1 Frost orb for free on turn one.

name: Claw
description: Deal ^3 damage. All Claw cards deal 2 additional damage this combat.
descriptionplus: Deal ^5 damage. All Claw cards deal 2 additional damage this combat.
statement: Claw is an incredibly divisive card among the community. It has the potential to scale extremely well, but before scaling is relatively unimpressive. Effects that allow you to play claw multiple times, such as hologram, reboot and all for one, can help to scale claw quickly before fights become overwhelming. Even when not trying to draught claw as a win condition, it is normally alright to pick one copy up early as a 0 cost card when you typically don't have any form of energy gain in act 1. Although it scales extremely slowly on its own, it can provide significant DPS in long boss battles, especially in skill heavy decks. Claw decks often run hello world because it can generate additional claws.

name: Cold Snap
description: Deal ^6 damage. Channel 1 Frost.
descriptionplus: Deal ^9 damage. Channel 1 Frost.
statement: Cold snap is a source of Frost and that is usually a good enough reason to pick it. Although there are other significantly better sources of Frost, often you cannot afford to be picky. It is good versus the gremlin nob as it provides a source of block through an attack.

name: Charge Battery
description: Gain ^7 Block. Next turn gain 1 [energy].
descriptionplus: Gain ^10 Block. Next turn gain 1 [energy].
statement: Charge battery is a decent source of block that also provides energy. It is good in act one, or if you have managed to make it to other acts without picking up many energy relics.

name: Consume
description: Gain ^2 Focus. Lose 1 Orb Slot.
descriptionplus: Gain ^3 Focus. Lose 1 Orb Slot.
statement: Since focus is incredibly rare, consume is actually an extremely powerful card. Its downside however is non-negligible, and you definitely need some sources are slot game in order to make consume worth it. You never need multiple copies of consume since it does not exhaust. Consume pairs best with inserter, as you can consume as many times as you like without ever having to worry about using up all of your orb slots.

name: Coolheaded
description: Channel 1 Frost. Draw ^1 card.
descriptionplus: Channel 1 Frost. Draw ^2 cards.
statement: Coolheaded is a brilliant card, especially moving into act two and act three. The draw is normally unimportant before you have acquired any energy relics but it's still welcome nonetheless. Frost typically grants about 8 or 10 block over the course of a fight, so this can be compared to shrug it off. Once you have enough focus, the Frost orbs become incredibly powerful.

name: Creative AI
description: At the start of each turn, add a random Power card to your hand.
descriptionplus: At the start of each turn, add a random Power card to your hand.
statement: Creative AI is a win condition and fits into the power archetype the defect has. Many of the defect’s powers trigger when playing other powers, such as storm, so this tends to spiral out of control quickly. If your deck is lacking any sort of direction or win condition, creative AI can come in handy. It obviously synergises very well with amplify. This card’s downside is that it is very slow and also very expensive so in hallway fights you might find yourself not able to play it. However, just like demon form, it can single-handedly turn the tide in boss battles. Note that this archetype is very heavily countered by the awakened, so consider playing slowly and holding back on this power until the awakened reaches phase 2.

name: Darkness
description: Channel 1 Dark.
descriptionplus: Channel 1 Dark. Trigger the passive ability of all Dark orbs.
statement: Although dark is a powerful orb, it is probably one of the most difficult to use effectively. It doesn't do any damage until it is evoked, and for maximum efficiency really needs to be played with dualcast or multicast. It can scale two very high numbers on boss encounters, which is important when trying to trigger a certain health threshold - for example, it is possible to kill the time eater before it does its half-health heal. I find the upgrade to be fairly unremarkable as well, as typically there will be other orbs active and not necessarily multiple dark orbs. Only take this if you are planning to make the most of dark or are severely lacking in DPS right before the first boss.

name: Defragment
description: Gain ^1 Focus.
descriptionplus: Gain ^2 Focus.
statement: Defragment is the only card source of focus with zero downsides. This makes it extremely valuable. Focus is a crazy powerful stat and stacking focus is a reliable game winning strategy at ascension 20, especially with a good number of Frost orbs that grants you nigh on invulnerability. I pick up almost every single defragment I see.

name: Doom and Gloom
description: Deal ^10 damage to ALL enemies. Channel 1 Dark.
descriptionplus: Deal ^14 damage to ALL enemies. Channel 1 Dark.
statement: Doom and gloom is decent in act one as it deals with the gremlins and the lice fairly effectively since it is a strong aoe attack. I consider the dark orb to be a bonus. It is designed in such a way that the small enemies are usually dead by the time the dark orb is channelled, allowing you to affectively take on an encounter with one large enemy and multiple smaller enemies. It is also one of the rare sources of dark that exist, so if your deck is well suited to dark orbs feel free to pick this up.

name: Double Energy
description: Double your Energy. Exhaust.
descriptionplus: Double your Energy. Exhaust.
statement: Double energy is a bit of a gamble. Sometimes its effect is completely negligible, as you do not have the cards to spend the energy generated. On the other hand, it can be extremely powerful, especially as you generate more energy through relics towards the end of the game. This card pairs particularly well with X-cost cards since you can guarantee that all of the energy that you create will be spent. Since it is a hit and miss card, I recommend pairing it with seek to ensure it is pulled on the right turn. The biggest combo for this card is playing double energy then another double energy then playing an X cost card such as storm.

name: Dualcast
description: Evoke your next Orb 2 times.
descriptionplus: Evoke your next Orb 2 times.
statement: This is a decent starter card which makes act one variable for the defect. I rarely upgrade dualcast unless I have an all for one in my deck. It is worth mentioning that if you get rid of your starter relic comma the cracked core, dualcast sometimes has no target that it can be used on. This makes swapping out your starter relic via Neow riskier. Of all of the orbs, dualcast works best with dark orbs, although plasma orbs are a close second, and of course it works well with all of them.

name: Echo Form
description: The first card you play each turn is played twice. ^Ethereal.
descriptionplus: The first card you play each turn is played twice.
statement: Insanely powerful, and a common card to end a winning run with. With two Echo Forms, by proccing Echo Form on Echo Form you can get 3 Echo Forms in play. This demolishes everything except the Time Eater. Only downsides are how expensive it is and the fact that it takes a turn to start working. If you see an echo form, pick it. If you see a second echo form pick that too.

name: Fission
description: Remove all of your Orbs. Gain [energy] and draw 1 card for each Orb removed. Exhaust.
descriptionplus: Evoke all of your Orbs. Gain [energy] and draw 1 card for each Orb Evoked. Exhaust.
statement: Fission is a fairly decent get out of jail card. On a dangerous turn, it can evoke all of your orbs 2 deal a lot of damage and generate a lot of block. The problem is that you now no longer have your orbs, So you typically have to use the draw and energy gain effects to replace the orbs that you spent. This isn't usually a problem, but if you draw fission too early you will have no orbs to evoke in the first place.  Note that I am assuming you have upgraded this card: if you pick this card you must upgrade it. No questions asked.

name: Force Field
description: Costs 1 less [energy] for each Power card played this combat. Gain ^12 Block.
descriptionplus: Costs 1 less [energy] for each Power card played this combat. Gain ^16 Block.
statement: If you are running 3 or 4 powers, force field is usually fine to take. In boss encounters it typically is a decent amount of block for 0 energy. It also works with creative AI obviously. This card is equivalent to a 2 energy card, so any cheaper is a bonus. Obviously, it is extremely difficult to guarantee that you will be able to discount this on the 1st cycle of your deck so it can sometimes be a dead draw.

name: FTL
description: Deal ^5 damage. If you have played less than ^3 cards this turn, draw 1 card.
descriptionplus: Deal ^6 damage. If you have played less than ^4 cards this turn, draw 1 card.
statement: This is a decent card that I always pick up over skipping, Although there often exist better choices. I would not recommend buying it in a shop as its upsides are not worth the cost. This card usually represents 5 free damage and it cycles - the only time this wouldn't happen is if you draw into it. note that it does not work very well with echo form, since you are able to quickly exceed the card threshold and you really don't want this card to be the one that is played twice.

name: Fusion
description: Channel 1 Plasma.
descriptionplus: Channel 1 Plasma.
statement: Fusion is an alright source of energy for the defect. I prefer to take it when I know that I have plenty of orb slots, since a typical defect deck will generate so many orbs that plasma is very quickly evoked and the sooner it is evoked the less value you get out of it. If I am lacking in energy relics, that is also another good reason to take it.

name: Genetic Algorithm
description: Gain 1 Block. When played, permanently increase this card's Block by ^2. Exhaust.
descriptionplus: Gain 1 Block. When played, permanently increase this card's Block by ^3. Exhaust.
statement: If I see a genetic algorithm in act one, I typically find myself picking it up. Bear in mind that it makes your deck considerably worse until it has been played four or five times, so if you are planning on taking a risky route with a lot of encounters or elites you should not be picking this up. When it is fully charged, it can be a huge source of block which is useful against some of the bigger bosses like the heart. You should not really pick up another copy after act 1. I normally limit myself to picking up two copies of this card to prevent myself dying from hallway fights.

name: Glacier
description: Gain ^7 Block. Channel 2 Frost.
descriptionplus: Gain ^10 Block. Channel 2 Frost.
statement: Glacier is a brilliant card, and one of the defect’s most powerful blocks. It is a solid block not only for this turned all the turns that follow. It also quickly generates orbs so prevent you having as many empty orb slots early on. I would always be happy to pick up two or maybe even 3 copies of glacier.

name: Go for the Eyes
description: Deal ^3 damage. If the enemy intends to attack, apply ^1 Weak.
descriptionplus: Deal ^4 damage. If the enemy intends to attack, apply ^2 Weak.
statement: This card is one of the defects only ways of applying weak. This is why I rate this card fairly highly, even though I think it compares poorly to other classes (such as Neutralize). It is useful in act 1 for preventing damage in combination with Frost orbs, and weak only becomes stronger as the enemies attacks increase in damage. It has an extremely unique interaction with Runic Dome, since it can be used to work out whether an enemy intends to attack or not.

name: Heatsinks
description: Whenever you play a Power card, draw ^1 card.
descriptionplus: Whenever you play a Power card, draw ^2 cards.
statement: Heatsinks is typically only taken in a creative AI deck, or one that runs a lot of powers in combination with storm. I would generally never pick this card, though I could understand getting it if you already had creative AI. it is normally something that I would want creative AI to generate rather than to draft in the deck.

name: Hello World
description: At the start of your turn, add a random Common card into your hand.
descriptionplus: ^Innate. At the start of your turn, add a random Common card into your hand.
statement: Good in the early game, not as powerful late. Is almost as good as an extra card draw every turn. The common cards for Defect are all solid, with the exception of a solitary Claw (but at 0 energy, I'll give it a pass). This begins to have a downside after your first shuffle, when your deck is filled with random commons instead of more powerful cards that have synergise with your decks. Can be used as a last resort if you have built a mainly offensive or defensive deck and need some of the other (e.g. a full frost deck with no damage).

name: Hologram
description: Gain ^3 Block. Return a card from your discard pile to your hand. ^Exhaust.
descriptionplus: Gain ^5 Block. Return a card from your discard pile to your hand.
statement: Hologram is an extremely powerful common card for the defect, although at first glance it looks fairly insignificant. I would happily take up to three or four holograms in my deck. Being able to pull any card out of your discard pile is incredibly powerful and makes piecing combo pieces together much more consistent. It is adaptive, allowing you to pull either defensive or offensive cards depending on what is required. Even without providing any block, this card would still be powerful. The defect has a crazy combo, where you can use two holograms and two copies of madness to make the holograms free and then generate infinite block by having the holograms pull each other out. This works very well against the heart or with relics such as letter opener.

name: Hyperbeam
description: Deal ^26 damage to ALL enemies. Lose 3 Focus.
descriptionplus: Deal ^34 damage to ALL enemies. Lose 3 Focus.
statement: Hyperbeam is a very powerful aoe attack with a serious downside. It can be used to tear through act one hallway fights very quickly, but as soon as you reach act 2 it becomes less consistent and the focus down begins to take its toll. I normally only consider taking this card if my deck does not rely on orbs at all, but almost every single defect deck does even to a small degree. The one that comes to mind is all for one. It can also be played with other focus down effects such as reprogram, since after losing a certain amount of focus anymore losses don't make any difference. Note that plasma is unaffected by focus.

name: Leap
description: Gain ^9 Block.
descriptionplus: Gain ^12 Block.
statement: A very unsexy form of block. It is solid and reliable and it is usually fine to pick this up early, although as the game goes on Frost orbs become more relevant.

name: Bullseye
description: Deal ^8 damage. Apply ^2 Lock-On.
descriptionplus: Deal ^11 damage. Apply ^3 Lock-On.
statement: Despite its name, lock on does not actually lock on to the target. Instead, it increases the damage that the target takes from lightning and dark orbs. I rarely find myself taking this card, as it is difficult to guarantee that you are hitting the right target or that you will have channelled enough orbs of the correct type for this to actually be effective. In theory, it can significantly increase a dark orb’s damage, but being able to cast this and evoke the orb on the same turn and on the right target is unlikely.

name: Loop
description: At the start of your turn, use the passive ability of your next Orb.
descriptionplus: At the start of your turn, use the passive ability of your next Orb ^2 times.
statement: Loop is an extremely powerful power. It grants you the passive bonus of an orb without requiring the slot or the orb’s generation. If you are struggling to generate orb slots, this is a fine alternative. Stacking loops can be very effective. When playing with loop, trying to ensure that by the end of the turn the orb in your front slot is the one that you want. I typically try to keep a Frost orb on the front slot to reliably generate block.

name: Machine Learning
description: Draw ^1 additional card at the start of each turn.
descriptionplus: Innate. Draw ^1 additional card at the start of each turn.
statement: Machine learning is an unimpressive rare power, but it's often better to take this over skipping. The draw can be difficult to appreciate that allows for much more consistent turns, though its overall effect is quite slow.

name: Melter
description: Remove all Block from an enemy. Deal ^10 damage.
descriptionplus: Remove all Block from an enemy. Deal ^14 damage.
statement: Melter have one extremely obvious target – the Spherical Guardian that appears in acts two and three. It is a one stop solution for destroying this enemy, similar to the silent’s use of poison. For this reason I usually only take one copy and get it during act 2 if possible. it is surprisingly easy to get value out of discard in other encounters as well, as a large amount of enemies do block. What's more, Melter actually does decent damage for 1 energy.

name: Meteor Strike
description: Deal ^24 damage. Channel 3 Plasma.
descriptionplus: Deal ^30 damage. Channel 3 Plasma.
statement: This card has such a low rating because it is extremely difficult to play. It requires two energy relics for you to be able to consistently play it when drawn. This often doesn't happen until Act 3. There are other sources of energy, such as charged battery and some non-boss relics, but these are extremely unreliable and rarely guarantee the energy on the turn it is required. If you have Snecko Eye, you should pick up every single meteor strike that you see as it changes the cost to 0-3.

name: Multi-Cast
description: Evoke your next Orb ^X times.
descriptionplus: Evoke your next Orb ^X+1 times.
statement: It can be difficult to get a lot of value out of multi-cast. This card works best with dark orbs that have accumulated a lot of damage. It can also work well with plasma to generate a very high amount of energy. This energy can then be spent on an X cost card if you have one in hand.

name: Overclock
description: Draw ^2 cards. Add a Burn into your discard pile.
descriptionplus: Draw ^3 cards. Add a Burn into your discard pile.
statement: Because overclock puts the burn cards into your discard pile, in many hallway fights you will normally never draw them, especially in larger decks. This card can be bad in long fights but with a lot of powers the damage is often negligible by the time you're set up and have drawn them. If you recycle the burns it can prevent them from building up in longer encounters. Overall a very solid card.

name: Rainbow
description: Channel 1 Lightning, 1 Frost, and 1 Dark. ^Exhaust.
descriptionplus: Channel 1 Lightning, 1 Frost, and 1 Dark.
statement: Rainbow gives you an easy way to quickly fill up your orb slots. If you can make good use of the orbs, it can be a decent amount of DPS with enough focus. When your powers and exhaustible cards are gone, you can play it fairly frequently so long as it is upgraded. With little focus, I would not consider upgrading it.

name: Reboot
description: Shuffle all of your cards into your draw pile, then draw ^4 cards. Exhaust.
descriptionplus: Shuffle all of your cards into your draw pile, then draw ^6 cards. Exhaust.
statement: The biggest upside for reboot is that it can always give you a new hand if your current cards are not sufficient. This means that I would always rather pick up a reboot than skipping a card completely. That said, a lot of the other rares are often better choices. Because this card shuffles your deck, it triggers relics that benefit from shuffling. As a side note, reboot helps you put good cards back into your draw pile. If you have already played the best half of your deck, reshuffling your draw pile increases the likelihood of you drawing these strong cards again. Conversely if you have played the worst half of your deck, it might be worth not reshuffling. this is especially relevant if you are waiting for a strong power that is still at the bottom of your deck. Because this card empties your discard pile, it has antisynergy with hologram.

name: Rebound
description: Deal ^9 damage. Put the next card you play this turn on top of your draw pile.
descriptionplus: Deal ^12 damage. Put the next card you play this turn on top of your draw pile.
statement: Rebound is an okay card which can be used well with claws and streamlines in order to scale them quickly. Since it allows you to guarantee drawing a card next turn, sometimes bouncing block is relevant. This card can be played last if you do not want about anything that is currently in your hand, such as strikes and defends.

name: Recursion
description: Evoke your next Orb. Channel the Orb that was just Evoked.
descriptionplus: Evoke your next Orb. Channel the Orb that was just Evoked.
statement: Recursion works best with dark orbs as they keep their stacks when they are re-evoked. As long as you have at least one or, recursion is never a dead draw. I usually prefer to upgrade Recursion as it can simply be played when drawn at 0 energy without much thought. However I would normally only pick this up if i'm running a dark deck.

name: Recycle
description: Exhaust a card. Gain [energy] equal to its cost.
descriptionplus: Exhaust a card. Gain [energy] equal to its cost.
statement: Recycle can be used to slim your deck down in long fights. The energy generation aspect of this card is usually irrelevant because your expensive cards are the ones that you do not want to be getting rid of. In some rare cases it can be used to exhaust for example a Sunder to great effect, but this case is fairly rare. More often, it will exhaust a strike or defend to prevent you from redrawing them. note that this card can also be used to get rid of wounds and burns. Although these cards do not provide any energy, sometimes it is more important to simply remove them from your deck. This is especially important with the Runic pyramid since wounds in particular do not discard ever.

name: Reinforced Body
description: Gain ^7 Block X times.
descriptionplus: Gain ^9 Block X times.
statement: Reinforced body is a solid block card. It is very flexible which comes at a slight cost to its efficiency. Since it blocks multiple times, it scales well with dexterity. I would always be happy have one or two in my deck.

name: Reprogram
description: Lose ^1 Focus. Gain 1 Strength. Gain 1 Dexterity.
descriptionplus: Lose ^2 Focus. Gain 2 Strength. Gain 2 Dexterity.
statement: Most of the time reprogram is way too slow to be effective. The downside is considerable, and the buff pales in comparison to inflame and footwork. A lot of the defects damage and defences come from orbs, and gimping your focus is usually worse than gaining strength and dexterity. On top of this, defect does not have many cards that actually benefit from strength - the main one being barrage, which ironically has antisynergy with focus down. Best when stacked or played multiple times at the cost of your orbs. Note that plasma orbs are not impacted by focus.

name: Rip and Tear
description: Deal ^7 damage to a random enemy 2 times.
descriptionplus: Deal ^9 damage to a random enemy 2 times.
statement: Rip and tear is a decent source of DPS in act one with the downside of having random targets. This downside doesn't matter at all in single target encounters. This card scales decently with strength. I would not pick any copies up after act one as they are too unreliable.

name: Scrape
description: Deal ^7 damage. Draw ^4 cards. Discard all cards drawn this way that do not cost 0.
descriptionplus: Deal ^10 damage. Draw ^5 cards. Discard all cards drawn this way that do not cost 0.
statement: Scrape works well in an All for one deck. It can be fine with a lot of 0 cost cards, but sometimes accidentally discarding an important power can ruin a run. It can even discard an All For One, so be careful when picking this up. Note that it can be used to discard curses and status effects that you know are on the top of your deck.

name: Seek
description: Put ^1 card from your draw pile into your hand. Exhaust.
descriptionplus: Put ^2 cards from your draw pile into your hand. Exhaust.
statement: Seek is a decent way of improving the consistency of your deck. When upgraded, it allows you to pull any two cards from your draw pile. With two upgraded copies of seek, you can draw any three cards from your draw pile by seeking your seek. This makes putting combo pieces together a breeze, such as a huge double energy turn with an X cost card. I would always pick up seek over sketching, but sometimes there are better rare cards available. Synergises exceptionally well with bottled lightning.

name: Self Repair
description: At the end of combat, heal ^7 HP.
descriptionplus: At the end of combat, heal ^10 HP.
statement: Self repair has an incredibly powerful effect. Heal is hard to come by in the defect and it’s a consistently large heal for cheap. I'm always happy to pick up one or two copies to negate chip damage taken in hallway fights. Note that the heal is not immediate so you need to be able to survive the encounter.

name: Skim
description: Draw ^3 cards.
descriptionplus: Draw ^4 cards.
statement: Works best with a few 0-cost cards, as in the early game paying for draw is the last thing you want to do. More effective late with some energy relics.

name: Stack
description: Gain Block equal to the number of cards in your discard pile.
descriptionplus: Gain Block equal to the number of cards in your discard pile ^+3.
statement: Better in large decks, quite obviously, and cards that increase the size of your deck. If drawn early, is worse than a defend, but in a deck of 30 cards can reliably reach 20. Hologram can help pull a whiffed early draw of Stack back into your hand when it is more useful.

name: Static Discharge
description: Whenever you receive unblocked attack damage, Channel ^1 Lightning.
descriptionplus: Whenever you receive unblocked  attack damage, Channel ^2 Lightning.
statement: Strong vs byrds, the Heart, and sometimes Hexaghost. With this card, try to block all but 1 damage (block for 12 when there is 13 damage incoming) in order to mitigate damage and still proc the power. Remember that frost orbs can be evoked during your enemies' turn. Brilliant with intangible effects. On the other hand, can push your frost orbs off which often leaves you vulnerable on subsequent turns.

name: Steam Barrier
description: Gain ^6 Block. Decrease this card's Block by 1 this combat.
descriptionplus: Gain ^8 Block. Decrease this card's Block by 1 this combat.
statement: Great in the early game and only fizzles out after multiple uses, likely only in boss battles. By the time this card has become ineffective, you will likely already have stacked orbs and powers.

name: Storm
description: Whenever you play a Power, Channel 1 Lightning.
descriptionplus: ^Innate. Whenever you play a Power, Channel 1 Lightning.
statement: Used with Creative AI.

name: Streamline
description: Deal ^15 damage. Reduce this card's cost by 1 this combat.
descriptionplus: Deal ^20 damage. Reduce this card's cost by 1 this combat.
statement: Streamline does a decent amount of damage, especially when upgraded. It can be difficult to play the first time, but then becomes extremely energy efficient as it gets cheaper. Hologram allows you to pull it on a nonthreatening turn for its initial cast, or pull it when already discounted as a cheap source of damage. Can even eventually be pulled by all for one. I typically take one copy in act one if I'm low on damage against elites or the boss.

name: Sunder
description: Deal ^24 damage. If this kills the enemy, gain [energy] [energy] [energy].
descriptionplus: Deal ^32 damage. If this kills the enemy, gain [energy] [energy] [energy].
statement: This card is fairly easy to trigger in act one but gets increasingly more difficult to use effectively as enemy health totals increase. Do not pick up any copies after act 1 unless you have Necronomicon.

name: Sweeping Beam
description: Deal ^6 damage to ALL enemies. Draw 1 card.
descriptionplus: Deal ^9 damage to ALL enemies. Draw 1 card.
statement: I try to pick up one copy early to provide some aoe damage versus gremlins, birds and lice. When you have energy relics, the draw can become relevant too. Generally not that impressive with lacklustre damage.

name: Tempest
description: Channel ^X Lightning. Exhaust.
descriptionplus: Channel ^X+1 Lightning. Exhaust.
statement: Tempest is about the same power level as a Zap but with more versatility. It can be useful for very quickly filling slots, and fits best into an electrodynamics deck. Double energy can allow you to pull off a huge Tempest as well.

name: Thunder Strike
description: Deal ^7 damage to a random enemy for each Lightning Channeled this combat.
descriptionplus: Deal ^9 damage to a random enemy for each Lightning Channeled this combat.
statement: Can be a strong finishing card in an electrodynamics deck or a static discharge deck. Generally strongest against a single-target, as you can reliably calculate who will take the damage (which is why it complements the aoe nature of electrodynamics so well).

name: TURBO
description: Gain [energy] [energy]. Add a Void into your discard pile.
descriptionplus: Gain [energy] [energy] [energy]. Add a Void into your discard pile.
statement: In most fights, the void never even gets drawn. Just make sure you are able to use the energy through card draw or more expensive cards.

name: White Noise
description: Add a random Power to your hand. It costs 0 this turn. Exhaust.
descriptionplus: Add a random Power to your hand. It costs 0 this turn. Exhaust.
statement: The Defect has some underwhelming powers. As a solo power, creating Storm or Heatsinks does nothing for the deck. Best case scenario is a 0-cost Echo Form.

name: Zap
description: Channel 1 Lightning.
descriptionplus: Channel 1 Lightning.
statement: Zap acts as fuel for dualcast early, and is your only way to evoke orbs at the start of the game. An early upgrade gives you a relevant 0 cost card which is good for act one and helps it fit into all for one decks. Sometimes with a full Frost deck you will eventually want to remove Zap to form a monochromatic deck.

name: Equilibrium
description: Gain ^13 Block. Retain your hand this turn.
descriptionplus: Gain ^16 Block. Retain your hand this turn.
statement: Equilibrium offers a solid block amount with a decent upside of retaining. I am always happy to have one - it can sometimes make it easier to assemble combo pieces. note that you cannot retain ethereal cards.

name: Compile Driver
description: Deal ^7 damage. Draw 1 card for each unique Orb you have.
descriptionplus: Deal ^10 damage. Draw 1 card for each unique Orb you have.
statement: Compile driver can draw a decent amount of cards, and very reliably draws at least one, putting it on par with quick slash. It is better from act 2 on with when you have a variety of orbs, more slots, and more energy to make use of the draw.

name: Electrodynamics
description: Lightning now hits ALL enemies. Channel ^2 Lightning.
descriptionplus: Lightning now hits ALL enemies. Channel ^3 Lightning.
statement: Electrodynamics is a brilliant card which offers extremely potent aoe. Even in the worst case scenario, it still generates orbs. Because the unique effect does not change, electrodynamics is not an upgrade priority. For the same reason, you should not take multiple copies of this card. It is very useful for making most hallway fights a breeze, particularly the Byrds and the Shapes.

name: Core Surge
description: Deal ^11 damage. Gain 1 Artifact. Exhaust.
descriptionplus: Deal ^15 damage. Gain 1 Artifact. Exhaust.
statement: Core Surge is often not good enough to pick over other rare cards. It offers middling damage, exhausts, and artifact is sometimes a wasted stat. It pairs well with biased cognition to prevent the focus down debuff. I would pick this over passing, but wouldn't normally want multiple copies.

name: Alpha
description: Shuffle a Beta into your draw pile. Exhaust.
descriptionplus: ^Innate. Shuffle a Beta into your draw pile. Exhaust.
statement: Alpha is an extremely powerful albeit slow ability. The first part of the chain is easy to play as it only costs 1 energy, but the two and three energy Beta and Omega that follow can be much more difficult to play without being punished. This is why it is recommended to only take this with energy relics or other sources of energy gain. Furthermore, it fits best into a thin deck in order to keep it consistent. Since it is quite slow, you might find that hallway fights don't require you to use this and in fact will make you take more damage if you do. The actual effect is devastating when it comes online and can finish most foes in two to three turns. It is also exceptionally powerful versus bosses with high health totals. This card is a build around card , usually requiring you to turtle with plenty of defence until it is ready to play. For this reason you often don't need any other sources of damage. It is very all or nothing, and is usually a poor addition to a large deck as it shuffles two useless cards into your deck that do nothing until all three are played. Additional draw effects and scry abilities can help you pull it off faster.

name: Battle Hymn
description: At the start of each turn, add a Smite into your hand.
descriptionplus: ^Innate. At the start of each turn, add a Smite into your hand.
statement: Battle hymn is a very consistent and cost efficient power that is a decent addition to most decks. Since the attacks that it generates retain, they can easily be played on a wrath turn as a big finisher. This is also the case for divinity. It is usually never bad to have one copy, but be aware that if you play 3 or more copies of this power you might not be able to empty your hand enough to actually draw on the next turn due to the retain effect.

name: Blasphemy
description: Enter Divinity. Die next turn. Exhaust
descriptionplus: ^Retain. Enter Divinity. Die next turn. Exhaust
statement: Although blasphemy might look terrible and frightening at first, the sheer strength of divinity makes this card worth it. When upgraded, you can enter divinity and gain 2 energy by doing so on any turn you like. This makes it a brilliant finisher. It is exceptionally powerful in hallway fights but obviously can be lacklustre in boss battles. Note that the death can be prevented by intangible or buffer, as the death is coded as one large hit of damage. Also note that the blasphemy status cannot be stopped with artifact (since it is actually coded as a buff not a debuff).

name: Bowling Bash
description: Deal ^7 damage for each enemy in combat.
descriptionplus: Deal ^10 damage for each enemy in combat.
statement: I like to take one copy of this card in my deck, particularly if I am offered one during act one. It makes multi enemy hallway fights a breeze if drawn early and can deal relevant damage in most boss fights as well. It's not exciting, but is a source of fast damage versus bandits, byrds or gremlins etc.

name: Brilliance
description: Deal ^12 damage. Deals additional damage equal to Mantra gained this combat.
descriptionplus: Deal ^16 damage. Deals additional damage equal to Mantra gained this combat.
statement: Brilliance is an all or nothing card. Typically, if you have enough sources of divinity brilliance is fine to take. It has okay damage for its cost even without any divinity, and tends to scale very quickly. note that if your deck is running divinity, it is usually a good idea to make sure your brilliance is played whilst in divinity for a huge hit. you will know if this card is good to take or not based on the rest of your deck. This card has a low rating overall as often other rares are better.

name: Carve Reality
description: Deal ^6 damage. Add a Smite to your hand.
descriptionplus: Deal ^10 damage. Add a Smite to your hand.
statement: Carve reality is an OK card that has fair damage. It isn't that spectacular, but its strength lies in being able to generate multiple smites . The smites will retain, allowing you to use them on a turn in wrath or in divinity for a big finisher. If this isn't how your deck works, I would recommend taking other sources of damage instead.

name: Collect
description: Put Miracle+ into your hand at the start of your next ^X turns. Exhaust.
descriptionplus: Put Miracle+ into your hand at the start of your next ^X+1 turns. Exhaust.

name: Conclude
description: Deal ^12 damage to ALL enemies. End your turn.
descriptionplus: Deal ^16 damage to ALL enemies. End your turn.
statement: Because conclude is so energy efficient, I often find myself picking this. It is fast damage that makes light work of hallway fights. Usually, the end turn effect isn't relevant as you can simply play it as your last card of the turn. On the other hand, This makes it difficult and risky to use in conjunction with wrath , as you must end the turn in wrath as well. Note that it also has terrible synergy with other end turn cards, so beware when taking multiple copies of conclude and other cards such as vault.

name: Conjure Blade
description: Shuffle an Expunger into your draw pile. Exhaust. (Expunger costs 1, deals 9 damage X times.)
descriptionplus: Shuffle an Expunger into your draw pile. Exhaust. (Expunger costs 1, deals 9 damage X+1 times.)
statement: Generally, this card is much more hassle than its worth, since you can spend all your turn's energy on a card that you might not even manage to draw. Even with a lot of damage on it, there are more reliable, fast-acting damage sources. Best in thin decks to get maximum uses. The more energy you can dump into it the better. Works well with miracles and energy relics.

name: Consecrate
description: Deal ^5 damage to ALL enemies.
descriptionplus: Deal ^8 damage to ALL enemies.
statement: Consecrate is a fast source of very cheap aoe damage. It works very well with wrath, and since it is so cheap it is not impossible to get in and out of wrath on the same turn as playing it. particularly good in act one before you've picked up any energy relics, but drops off considerably in the later acts. I would not recommend picking more than one of these.

name: Crescendo
description: Retain. Enter Wrath. Exhaust.
descriptionplus: Retain. Enter Wrath. Exhaust.
statement: Crescendo is a brilliant source of wrath. It has retain by default and when upgraded can be played for free. Since it retains, it can be used on the final turn of combat without any concern for retaliation damage. The only downside to this card is that it exhausts, and in some cases you might want up to two copies of crescendo have since other sources of wrath do not retain.

name: Crush Joints
description: Deal ^8 damage. If the last card played this combat was a Skill, apply ^1 Vulnerable.
descriptionplus: Deal ^10 damage. If the last card played this combat was a Skill, apply ^2 Vulnerable.
statement: Crush joints is a difficult card to play since you need to play a skill beforehand. Skills tend to be defensive, and attacks offensive, so this is intentionally designed to be awkward. Note that miracle classes as a skill. Since this card only applies one stack of vulnerable it might not look that valuable, but it is important to remember that wrath and divinity are greatly enhanced by vulnerable, closing causing wrath to deal 3x the damage and divinity to deal 4.5x the damage.

name: Cut Through Fate
description: Deal ^7 damage. Scry ^2. Draw 1 card.
descriptionplus: Deal ^9 damage. Scry ^3. Draw 1 card.
statement: Cut through fate is an exceptionally strong common card for the watcher. Not only does it provide a draw, but it also allows you two carefully decide which of the top three cards you want to draw. Scrying away strikes and defends happens very frequently, and the scribe is often the difference between drawing enough damage to kill a small creature and not.

name: Deceive Reality
description: Gain ^4 Block. Add a Safety to your hand.
descriptionplus: Gain ^7 Block. Add a Safety to your hand.
statement: The power of Deceive reality lies in the retain keyword on the block that it generates. Being able to store up a number of blocks with retain is sometimes exceptionally important, particularly against bosses such as the Guardian and the champ who have turns with scary amounts of burst damage. It is also still fine in hallway fights, as it means you have block when you need it and can otherwise draft more offensively. Note that this card is affected by dexterity twice.

name: Deus Ex Machina
description: Unplayable. When you draw this card, add ^2 Miracles to your hand and Exhaust.
descriptionplus: Unplayable. When you draw this card, add ^3 Miracles to your hand and Exhaust.
statement: A bit slow, but okay to take if you have no energy relics. Best supported by decent draw cards so you can make use of the energy, especially on the turn that this triggers.

name: Deva Form
description: ^Ethereal. At the start of your turn, gain [energy] and increase this gain by 1.
descriptionplus: At the start of your turn, gain [energy] and increase this gain by 1.

name: Devotion
description: At the start of your turn, gain ^2 Mantra.
descriptionplus: At the start of your turn, gain ^3 Mantra.
statement: Devotion fits very well into mantra heavy decks. It allows you to predict when you will proc divinity, as it does not rely on you drawing a mantra card. This can also be a downside, as sometimes you will have nine stacks of mantra and force yourself to enter divinity next turn whether you want it or not. This can be devastating if you do not draw any attacks on the turn that this happens. Generally speaking, it is very energy efficient and easy to play without being punished and several of this power stacked can ensure that you enter divinity every single turn which is not to be underestimated.

name: Empty Body
description: Gain ^7 Block. Exit your Stance.
descriptionplus: Gain ^10 Block. Exit your Stance.
statement: Empty body is not a very impressive card. It doesn't provide a great deal of block and also doesn't have much synergy with any of the stances. At best, it allows you to leave wrath at the end of a turn or to cash in the energy that is generated when you leave calm. There are better sources of block, so I typically pass on this card.

name: Empty Fist
description: Deal ^9 damage. Exit your Stance.
descriptionplus: Deal ^14 damage. Exit your Stance.
statement: Of the three exit cards, empty fest has the best synergy with wrath. It has reasonable damage, especially when doubled or tripled.  Since the damage is dealt before you leave your stance, it is great to play as the final card off the turn, allowing you to fully benefit from damage stances without leaving yourself vulnerable. Note that exit is not that useful when running a divinity deck.

name: Empty Mind
description: Draw ^2 cards. Exit your Stance.
descriptionplus: Draw ^3 cards. Exit your Stance.
statement: Empty mind is perhaps the most powerful of the three exit cards. It provides a great deal of draw, and when leaving com also generates energy to allow you to play the cards that you draw. It is common to play empty mind with deva form since it provides so much draw and allows you to spend the large amounts of energy that are generated with this power.

name: Eruption
description: Deal 9 damage. Enter Wrath.
descriptionplus: Deal 9 damage. Enter Wrath.
statement: Since eruption is the only source of wrath that you start with in the watcher, you do not want to remove this until you have drafted another source. It is clunky to use since it costs quite a lot of energy whilst not dealing very much damage, and being left in wrath leaves you open to counter attacks. Since the damage happens before you enter wrath, the damage is not even doubled. If you draught another source of wrath, in particular tantrum, it is then common to remove eruption from your deck. If you are planning to remove eruption, it is not recommended that you upgrade it. note that if you end the turn in wrath, you open yourself two more damage, not only on this turn but also all subsequent turns until you draw a source of calm. If Tranquilly is in your discard pile, take care when deciding to play eruption.

name: Establishment
description: Whenever a card is Retained, reduce its cost by 1 this combat.
descriptionplus: ^Innate. Whenever a card is Retained, reduce its cost by 1 this combat.
statement: Since there are so many top tier cards with the retain keyword, establishment can be an exceptionally strong power. It is cheap to play and pays for itself within one or two turns generally. It works brilliantly with battle hymn as a consistent source of free damage. Although this card is rated highly, do make sure that your deck has a decent number of retain cards, otherwise this power will be worthless.

name: Evaluate
description: Gain ^6 Block. Shuffle an Insight into your draw pile.
descriptionplus: Gain ^10 Block. Shuffle an Insight into your draw pile.
statement: Evaluate is a solid source of block with an upside. It allows you to draw more cards than normal, and you can best take advantage of this by ensuring you have a lot of sources of energy in your deck. This might mean having copies of Deus Ex machina, Deva form, or Collect in your deck. Since it is also a skill that is free, it works well with relics such as letter opener. At worst, it gives you more consistent hands, especially since insight has retain.

name: Fasting
description: Gain ^3 Strength. Gain ^3 Dexterity. Gain 1 less [energy] at the start of each turn.
descriptionplus: Gain ^4 Strength. Gain ^4 Dexterity. Gain 1 less [energy] at the start of each turn.
statement: Fasting is a very niche power that is only usually taken in decks that can negate the energy loss. orange pellets are capable of removing the debuff, and artifact also blocks the debuff from being applied. I definitely would not recommend taking fasting without at least one energy relic or means of negating the debuff. The strength and dexterity are nice but typically having one extra energy what do the same thing, whilst allowing you to be more flexible with your turns. Note that sources of strength are rare for the watcher since wrath and divinity benefit from this multiple times.

name: Fear No Evil
description: Deal ^8 damage. If the enemy intends to Attack, enter Calm.
descriptionplus: Deal ^11 damage. If the enemy intends to Attack, enter Calm.
statement: Fear no evil is a strong and consistent attack that allows you to cheaply enter calm. Its strength lies in its flexibility. Typically, you only want to enter calm and leave wrath when you are being attacked. The biggest downside of taking this card is sometimes forgetting that your target must be attacking in order to put you into calm. On more than one occasion, I have killed a small minion that is not attacking and left myself in wrath when I didn't mean to.

name: Flurry Of Blows
description: Deal ^4 damage. Whenever you change stances, return this from the discard pile to your hand.
descriptionplus: Deal ^6 damage. Whenever you change stances, return this from the discard pile to your hand.
statement: Synergises with your starter cards. Note that the card has to be in your discard pile in order for it to return to your hand. If on the same turn you can draw a card which will re-shuffle your deck, make sure you play this card AFTER the reshuffle so that it goes straight into the new discard pile. This card works with Calm, Wrath, Divinity, and Exit. Strategies relying on this card can be difficult against the Time Lord and the final boss.

name: Flying Sleeves
description: Retain. Deal ^4 damage twice.
descriptionplus: Retain. Deal ^6 damage twice.
statement: Flying sleeves is a solid filler card. Although it doesn't deal a great amount of damage, the fact that it retains allows you to play it on turns where you are in wrath or divinity. Also, since it has a multi attack, it benefits more from strength than most other cards. Although I wouldn't pick more than one of these, having one copy for act one is usually fine.

name: Follow-Up
description: Deal ^7 damage. If the last card played this combat was an Attack, gain [energy].
descriptionplus: Deal ^11 damage. If the last card played this combat was an Attack, gain [energy].
statement: Would you play a 0 cost attack that dealt 7 damage? This is the best case scenario, and it comes with a condition. Whilst it can be fine and isn't usually that difficult to execute, too many copies of this card prevent you from effectively spending all of your energy and the damage isn't spectacular. I would pick one at most in act one and leave it at that. What with the watcher’s multiple ways of manipulating energy and stances, often cards must be sequenced very specifically, which doesn't leave you with the one energy to play this card.

name: Foreign Influence
description: Choose 1 of 3 Attacks of any color to add into your hand. Exhaust.
descriptionplus: Choose 1 of 3 Attacks of any color to add into your hand. It costs ^0 this turn. Exhaust.
statement: More often than not, foreign influence is a bad card. When discovering cards from your own class, there is a much higher chance of drafting something that synergises with your deck. Since this card can generate options from any classes, you rarely find what you are looking for. Normally it is nice to benefit from the card costing zero the first time it is played, allowing you to lean towards the more expensive options, but in many cases cards are offered that will do nothing at all when you're playing as the watcher which doesn't allow you to be as picky. (For example, catalyst.)

name: Foresight
description: At the start of your turn, Scry 3.
descriptionplus: At the start of your turn, Scry ^4.
statement: Foresight is one of the strongest powers the watcher has at her disposal. Although it might look unimpressive, scry allows you to very consistently draw the cards that you want, which becomes even more evident as you begin to learn enemy movesets. It works well with Alpha, as it allows you to quickly sift through your deck and get Omega online. Furthermore, since you scry every single turn, any cards that benefit from a scry effect such as Weave benefit greatly from this card. I would always take one of these over passing.

name: Halt
description: Gain ^3 Block. If you are in Wrath, gain ^9 additional Block.
descriptionplus: Gain ^4 Block. Wrath: Gain ^14 additional Block.
statement: At first glance, Halt might look unimpressive. However, after trying it out, you will find that in many scenarios the additional block generated by this card allows you to stay in wrath at the end of a turn without being too heavily punished. This is particularly the case in act one where the enemies do not have as hard hitting attacks. I would not take this card unless I had consistent sources of wrath, for example a Tantrum. In the worst case scenario, this still provides some free block no matter what stance you are in.

name: Indignation
description: If you are in Wrath, apply ^3 Vulnerable to ALL enemies, otherwise enter Wrath.
descriptionplus: If you are in Wrath, apply ^5 Vulnerable to ALL enemies, otherwise enter Wrath.
statement: Indignation is an awkward card. Typically, once you are in wrath, every single point of energy matters as you need to make sure that any attacking enemies die unless you plan on leaving the stance on the same turn. There are much more energy efficient and consistent sources of entering wrath, so the only reason to take this card is to apply the heavy vulnerable debuff to the enemies. Vulnerable does stack extremely well with wrath, so this effect can be devastating particularly in longer fights. However, such circumstances tend to make this card to hindrance more often than a help.

name: Inner Peace
description: If you are in Calm, draw ^3 cards. Otherwise, enter Calm.
descriptionplus: If you are in Calm, draw ^4 cards. Otherwise, enter Calm.
statement: Inner peace is a cheap way to enter calm or draw cards. the draw is extremely energy efficient, and although there are better sources of calm sometimes it is all you need to make sure you can get in and out of wrath on the same turn. The draw effect is most powerful when you have a considerable amount of energy, typically because of a collect or deva form.

name: Judgment
description: If the enemy has ^30 or less HP, set their HP to 0.
descriptionplus: If the enemy has ^40 or less HP, set their HP to 0.
statement: Great against Spherical Sentry but multiple copies can clutter your deck. Usually performs worst in boss battles where it can be almost impossible to play.

name: Just Lucky
description: Scry ^1. Gain ^2 Block. Deal ^3 damage.
descriptionplus: Scry ^2. Gain ^3 Block. Deal ^4 damage.
statement: Generally only take early in Act 1 or in Scry based decks. As soon as you have picked up an energy relic, you will often find yourself unable to spend all of your energy on a turn. Although this card scries, unlike cut through fate it doesn't then draw the card.

name: Lesson Learned
description: Deal ^10 damage. If Fatal, Upgrade a random card in your deck. Exhaust.
descriptionplus: Deal ^13 damage. If Fatal, Upgrade a random card in your deck. Exhaust.
statement: Better the earlier you get it. Note that the upgrades are permanent, not just for this encounter, and that the encounter does not benefit from the upgrade. If you pick up this card in act one, it is not uncommon to finish with a fully upgraded deck. When you have this card, consider taking more hallway fights than you normally would since it allows you to permanently upgrade a card at low risk. Although it might look silly to upgrade this, if it allows you to more consistently get an upgrade in your deck it is easily worth it. For obvious reasons, this card synergises extremely well with Fusion hammer.

name: Like Water
description: At the end of your turn, if you are in Calm, gain ^5 Block.
descriptionplus: At the end of your turn, if you are in Calm, gain ^7 Block.
statement: Like water is a very powerful effect. It essentially acts like Metallicize so long as you stay in calm. One copy is great, and multiple copies can make you nearly invincible. It is not uncommon to remove all sources of wrath ifs running multiple copies of this power. Note that it does not synergise very well with mantra cards, as it can be difficult to re-enter calm on a turn where you enter divinity.

name: Master Reality
description: Whenever a card is created during combat, Upgrade it.
descriptionplus: Whenever a card is created during combat, Upgrade it.
statement: Master reality is another niche but incredibly strong power. It works best with battle hymn, as the card that is generated every single turn is upgraded. It obviously works well with any cards that create another card, but it works best with dead branch, especially since many of the cards that get created in the watcher are also then exhausted themselves. This is a game breaking combination. On the other hand, many decks do not require or benefit from master reality, so make sure you have enough create effects to make this power worth it.

name: Meditate
description: Put ^a card from your discard pile into your hand and Retain it. Enter Calm. End your turn.
descriptionplus: Put ^2 cards from your discard pile into your hand and Retain them. Enter Calm. End your turn.

name: Mental Fortress
description: Whenever you change Stances, gain ^4 Block.
descriptionplus: Whenever you change Stances, gain ^6 Block.
statement: Mental fortress is a build around card that requires you to take many stance change effects. Note that exit also counts as a change of stance. Obviously, this card synergises extremely well with flurry of blows, as not only are you generating block for changing stances, but most of the time you will also drawing an additional attack. Multiple copies of this make the effect even stronger, in many cases meaning you don't need to use block cards. Note that this strategy can be fairly inconsistent, as if you do not draw the stance change cards that you need you will often die on the same turn. I would not include mantra cards when employing this kind of strategy.

name: Nirvana
description: Whenever you Scry, gain ^3 Block.
descriptionplus: Whenever you Scry, gain ^4 Block.
statement: Nirvana is and okay card that works best in scry decks. These decks usually take up to three copies of weave as their main source of damage. This card obviously synergises extremely well with foresight, as it allows you to start the turn with block, essentially acting like metallicize. Typically, I wouldn't take this card unless I already had foresight.

name: Omniscience
description: Choose a card in your draw pile. Play the chosen card twice and Exhaust it. Exhaust.
descriptionplus: Choose a card in your draw pile. Play the chosen card twice and Exhaust it. Exhaust.
statement: Although omniscience can be a difficult card to play, it can also be completely game winning. The high energy cost means that in many cases you need to have an energy relic or have it upgraded in order to be able to play it. However, this is not much of a downside as usually you won't be able to find this card until act two. Omniscience is at its best when you have two copies in the deck: It allows you to more consistently draw an omniscience early, and omniscience can be played on the other copy of omniscience, actually allowing you to play TWO cards twice. This is an extremely powerful effect, especially when combined with sources of mantra, as you can often enter divinity on turn 1 using this strategy.

name: Perseverance
description: Retain. Gain ^5 Block. When Retained, increase its Block by ^2 this combat.
descriptionplus: Retain. Gain ^7 Block. When Retained, increase its Block by ^3 this combat.
statement: In practise, perseverance is a difficult card to make use of. You normally want to play a block card every single turn, and if this is the only source of block that you have drawn then you cannot afford to hold on to it. Thus, unless you are playing a fairly defensive deck in the first place it can be difficult to actually allow this to stack. Note that it does have its purpose, and is particularly good versus the big slime and the Guardian bosses that have huge attack turns In addition to turns where they don't attack at all. Note that the block gain persists throughout combat, meaning that the second time you draw it, it keeps all of the stacks that it had previously.

name: Pray
description: Gain ^3 Mantra. Shuffle an Insight into your draw pile.
descriptionplus: Gain ^4 Mantra. Shuffle an Insight into your draw pile.
statement: Pray is given a low tier rating due to the fact that on its own it does very little. Unlike prostrate, it does not provide any block and also comes with an energy cost. On the other hand, the insight can be useful for quickly cycling through your deck to attain divinity faster than usual. This card is fine as a supplement to an already stable mantra deck, but I rate it as one of the weaker ones unless you can make great use of the insights.

name: Pressure Points
description: Apply ^8 Mark. ALL enemies lose HP equal to their Mark.
descriptionplus: Apply ^11 Mark. ALL enemies lose HP equal to their Mark.
