statement: Pressure points is a very unique mechanic that unfortunately can be quite unwieldy. it is most effective during boss fights where there is one enemy with a high health total that takes more and more damage with each use. In hallway fights, it can be difficult to make use of this card due to the fact that you normally want to kill enemies with a low health total first to get rid of them and reduce incoming damage. It is likely that the first enemy that you target with this ability will be dead by the time you draw it a second time. For this reason, I rate it quite lowly. Even when I've been able to draught 3 copies in a fairly slim deck, I have still found it to be ineffective. I think one copy is fine, two has potential, but you really shouldn't pick any more especially at higher ascension.

name: Prostrate
description: Gain ^2 Mantra. Gain 4 Block.
descriptionplus: Gain ^3 Mantra. Gain 4 Block.
statement: Prostrate is a decent source of mantra. It is free, and also grants you blank, making it worthwhile to use even in fights where you don't reach divinity. Note that one prostrate on its own will very rarely get you into divinity since unupgraded it must be played five times and when upgraded must be played four. This is fine to pick as your first mantra card so long as you plan on taking more.

name: Protect
description: Retain. Gain ^12 Block.
descriptionplus: Retain. Gain ^16 Block.
statement: Protect is a very solid source of block. It is not uncommon to draw more block cards than you need on a turn, and in these cases being able to retain a block card it's very useful for preventing chip damage. The block amount is decent for the energy cost. This card is particularly important versus encounters with hard hitting attacks, such as the large slime and the Guardian bosses. I would always be happy to have a couple of copies of this in my deck.

name: Ragnarok
description: Deal ^5 damage to a random enemy ^5 times.
descriptionplus: Deal ^6 damage to a random enemy ^6 times.
statement: Ragnarok can be a powerful card in the right circumstances, but more often than not it is difficult to play. Against single target encounters, it can be extremely powerful since it has focused fire. On the other hand, against a boss like DECA and donate, the split damage can be the difference between winning and losing. Ragnarok has some very specific synergies: it benefits greatly from strength, wreath of flame effectively doubles the damage, and omniscience allows it to be played multiple times.

name: Reach Heaven
description: Deal ^10 damage. Shuffle a Through Violence into your draw pile.
descriptionplus: Deal ^15 damage. Shuffle a Through Violence into your draw pile.
statement: Reach heaven can be a powerful card in the right circumstances. It's quite slow, which means that it's not normally that effective in hallway fights unless playing against an enemy that scales quite slowly. Due to its high cost and low reward, many times you will find that you are unable to play it.  Since through violence has retain, it is common to use it with wrath or divinity for a huge hit.

name: Rushdown
description: Whenever you enter Wrath, draw 2 cards.
descriptionplus: Whenever you enter Wrath, draw 2 cards.
statement: Although rushdown might look like it has a fairly insignificant effect, it allows you to enter wrath more freely. Oftentimes it is a gamble when you enter wrath whether you will be able to leave again on the following turn which can open you up to a lot of damage. This power gives you a few extra chances to draw hard hitting attacks that can finish combat there and then, or on the other hand allows you to draw a calm card to end the turn with.

name: Sanctity
description: Gain ^6 Block. If the last card played was a Skill, draw 2 cards.
descriptionplus: Gain ^9 Block. If the last card played was a Skill, draw 2 cards.
statement: Sanctity can be an okay card as long as you have the energy to actually make use of the draw effect. The block that it grants is insignificant, and the draw effect has a condition attached to it. It is worth noting that the condition can be satisfied if you finished your last turn by playing a skill. Because of this come out it is recommended that you always finish your turns with a skill where possible.

name: Sands of Time
description: Retain. Deal ^20 damage. When Retained, lower its cost by 1 this combat.
descriptionplus: Retain. Deal ^26 damage. When Retained, lower its cost by 1 this combat.
statement: Sands of time is a slow card but one with a lot of damage. It can normally be played after being held in your hand for two or three turns, and if you can afford to hold it for four turns it becomes free for the rest of combat. Note that the next time you draw this card it will continue counting down from the cost that you last played it at. This makes it a strong source of consistent damage in longer boss fights. Due to the retain effect, it is easy to use sands of time on a turn where you are in wrath or divinity.

name: Sash Whip
description: Deal ^8 damage. If the last card played this combat was an Attack, apply ^1 Weak.
descriptionplus: Deal ^10 damage. If the last card played this combat was an Attack, apply ^2 Weak.
statement: Sash whip is one of the few sources of week that exists in the class. For this reason, I usually pick up one or two copies, no matter what act I am on. Weak continues to scale very well into the late game. This card can be quite awkward to play, since the card played before it must be an attack, and if you are applying weak you typically want to be playing skill to prevent incoming damage. Note that if you end your turn with an attack, sash whip will start already active on your next turn. If your deck has multiple copies of sash whip, it is recommended that you try to finish turns with an attack where possible.

name: Scrawl
description: Draw cards until your hand is full. Exhaust.
descriptionplus: Draw cards until your hand is full. Exhaust.
statement: Scrawl is an extremely powerful card that increases the consistency of your deck. It allows you to quickly draw your most potent cards, such as a ragnarok or omniscience. I would always take scrawl over skipping, even if this meant having multiple copies of scrawl.

name: Signature Move
description: Can only be played if this is the only Attack in your hand. Deal ^30 damage.
descriptionplus: Can only be played if this is the only Attack in your hand. Deal ^40 damage.
statement: Signature move is an extremely difficult card to pull off. On top of this, the damage that it deals is not particularly exceptional. Compare this to grand finale - grand finale deals more damage, and that damage is aoe, and on top of this it doesn't have any cost. Even on turns where this is the only attack that is drawn, it can be difficult to find the energy to play it out. In theory, as long as you play all the attacks in your hand you will be able to play this, which means you don't have to gimp your deck by picking very few attacks. On the other hand, its high cost means playing out more than one attack before this card can be difficult, and attacks that retain make this even harder to pull off. Note that you should never put multiple copies of signature move in your deck, as if two are drawn on the same turn there is no way to play either of them.

name: Simmering Fury
description: At the start of your next turn, enter Wrath and draw ^2 cards.
descriptionplus: At the start of your next turn, enter Wrath and draw ^3 cards.
statement: Since simmering fury now also draws you cards on the turn that you enter wrath, it is much more reliable. It gives you an increased likelihood of being able to finish the encounter on the next turn so long as you draw the right attacks. Due to the unpredictable nature of these draws, I tend to err on the side of caution and skip simmering fury, but that is not to say that it is a weak card. It is a cheap source of wrath, and you pay the energy cost in advance, allowing you to dedicate more energy to attacks on your wrath turn. This is a particularly reliable strategy with cards such as battle hymn once you have accumulated enough attacks with retain.

name: Spirit Shield
description: Gain ^3 Block for each card in your hand.
descriptionplus: Gain ^4 Block for each card in your hand.
statement: Spirit shield is one of the strongest cards at the watcher’s disposal. It very consistently generates a lot of block, particularly due to how many of the watcher’s cards have retain. This even includes the miracle that you obtain due to your starting relic. I don't think you can ever have too many copies.

name: Study
description: At the end of your turn, shuffle an Insight into your draw pile.
descriptionplus: At the end of your turn, shuffle an Insight into your draw pile.
statement: Study can be a strong power in the right deck, however it normally requires you to have a lot of sources of energy. It synergises particularly well with deva form by generating a draw engine In addition to an energy engine. It can be difficult to play if it is an upgraded due to its high cost for no immediate effect. Study obviously synergises with relics that trigger based off skills, such as letter opener.

name: Swivel
description: Gain ^8 Block. The next Attack you play costs 0.
descriptionplus: Gain ^11 Block. The next Attack you play costs 0.
statement: Swivel can be powerful in the right circumstances, however in general I find that the watcher does not have that many expensive attacks. A lot of the cheap attacks are common unstrung, often meaning that the discount goes to waste. This card obviously synergises extremely well with expensive attacks, most notably ragnarok. Note that this effect carries across multiple turns, so it is possible to use the card at the end of the turn if the attacks that are currently in your hand are not that expensive.

name: Talk to the Hand
description: Deal ^5 damage. Whenever you attack this enemy, gain ^2 Block. Exhaust.
descriptionplus: Deal ^7 damage. Whenever you attack this enemy, gain ^3 Block. Exhaust.
statement: Talk to the hand is one of my favourite watcher cards. It allows you to play very offensively while still maintaining a defence. It synergises extremely well with itself, allowing you to generate upwards of 20 block just by using attacks every single turn. The effect is triggered multiple times by multi hit attacks, making cards like ragnarok very synergistic. Although in shorter combats with multiple low health enemies this card is less effective, it still acts as a source of damage and can be extremely effective versus elites and bosses. Note that since it is a debuff, bosses with transformations will be able to cleanse this effect. If I see talk to the hand, I almost always take it.

name: Tantrum
description: Deal 3 damage ^3 times. Enter Wrath. Shuffle this card into your draw pile.
descriptionplus: Deal 3 damage ^4 times. Enter Wrath. Shuffle this card into your draw pile.
statement: Tantrum is an extremely powerful and consistent card. It is quite possibly the best source of wrath in the game. Since it shuffles back into your deck you can always guarantee that you will draw another source of wrath soon. It is not uncommon to play tantrum and draw it again the next turn. The upside of this is you are already in wrath, so tantrum’s damage is doubled. The fact that it hits multiple times means that it benefits greatly from strength. Note that sometimes decks choose to completely avoid wrath, particularly divinity decks. However, 90% of the time it is correct to have one or two copies of tantrum in your deck. This card is better than eruption in every possible sense, and it is common to remove eruption after drafting tantrum.

name: Third Eye
description: Gain ^7 Block. Scry ^3.
descriptionplus: Gain ^9 Block. Scry ^5.
statement: Although third eye is not particularly flashy, it offers a solid amount of block and the scry effect is not to be overlooked. The only thing that would make this card better is if it also drew. Note that newer players will struggle to predict what the enemy is going to do on the next turn, and this can make it difficult to know which cards to scry away and which cards to keep. In the worst case scenario, it is usually a good idea to get rid of any strikes or defends that you find, as literally any other cards in your deck will be better. The better you know your opponent, the more effective this card will be. If, for example, you know that the enemy will not be attacking next turn, you should remove any of your defensive cards and blocks (and vice versa).

name: Tranquility
description: Retain. Enter Calm. Exhaust.
descriptionplus: Retain. Enter Calm. Exhaust.
statement: Tranquillity is such a powerful card due to its consistency. Since it has retain, it means you can enter wrath more liberally than usual, as you have a backup plan in case you have no way of exiting wrath or finishing your opponent next turn. It can even be useful to play on the same turn as wrath after playing your attacks to prevent the enemy from hitting back as hard on their turn. The only downside to tranquilly is the fact that it exhausts - if this is your only source of calm, you will only be able to enter it once. For this reason, it is not uncommon to pick up even 2 copies of this card in addition to other sources of calm such as vigilance.

name: Vault
description: Take an extra turn after this one. End your turn. Exhaust.
descriptionplus: Take an extra turn after this one. End your turn. Exhaust.
statement: Good with end of turn ramping effects such as Deva Form. On the Time Lord, skips timewarp if played as 12th card. Can be used to wear off your debuffs (just be wary that it skips your buffs too, like intangible) [TBC!]. If nothing else, this card can be used to refill your hand when you get a bad draw.

name: Vigilance
description: Gain ^8 Block. Enter Calm.
descriptionplus: Gain ^12 Block. Enter Calm.
statement: Vigilance is a very important card for the watcher starting deck. It provides a decent amount of block and is the only source of calm that the watcher starts with. Although it is fairly energy inefficient, I rarely find myself needing to remove this card. I definitely would not remove vigilance unless I had another source of calm that does not exhaust.

name: Wallop
description: Deal ^9 damage. Gain Block equal to unblocked damage dealt.
descriptionplus: Deal ^12 damage. Gain Block equal to unblocked damage dealt.
statement: Note that overkilling an enemy with wallop will only grant block up to the actual damage dealt.

name: Wave of the Hand
description: Whenever you gain Block this turn, apply ^1 Weak to ALL enemies.
descriptionplus: Whenever you gain Block this turn, apply ^2 Weak to ALL enemies.

description: Deal ^4 damage. Whenever you Scry, return this from the discard pile to your Hand.
descriptionplus: Deal ^6 damage. Whenever you Scry, return this from the discard pile to your Hand.

description: Deal ^15 damage. Draw 2 cards.
descriptionplus: Deal ^20 damage. Draw 2 cards.

name: Windmill Strike
description: Retain. Deal ^7 damage. When Retained, increase its damage by ^4 this combat.
descriptionplus: Retain. Deal ^10 damage. When Retained, increase its damage by ^5 this combat.
statement: Can serve as a win-condition. The +damage effect is doubled when you take wrath into account (+10 per turn upgraded), or tripled if you're running a divinity deck (+15 per turn upgraded). Its retain effect makes it easy to play on wrath/divinity turns so it makes a great finisher.

name: Wish
description: Choose one: Gain ^6 Plated Armor, ^3 Strength, or ^25 Gold. Exhaust.
descriptionplus: Choose one: Gain ^8 Plated Armor, ^4 Strength, or ^30 Gold. Exhaust.
statement: not power vs awakened, omni, strength better in watcher (fasting only other), win-more for gold in turtle decks, plated armor in emergencies

name: Worship
description: Gain 5 Mantra.
descriptionplus: ^Retain. Gain 5 Mantra.
statement: Although worship is quite an expensive card which does nothing the first time it's played, when it is upgraded it is considerably more effective. By giving this card retain, you are able to enter divinity on whichever turn you see fit. When you enter divinity, the cost of the card will be refunded so this isn't too much of a problem. Furthermore, one or two copies of this card can serve all of your mantra needs. Many of the other mantra cards offer so little that you need to stack several of them in order to be able to reach divinity before the end of a fight. Even if worship is the only mantra card you have, it can still work out. It has a low rating since it is quite a slow card, but if your deck consistently benefits from damage amplification, this card can be worth it in the long run.

name: Wreath of Flame
description: Your next Attack deals ^5 additional damage.
descriptionplus: Your next Attack deals ^8 additional damage.
statement: Wreath of flame is quite a difficult card to analyse but it definitely has more uses than it may first seem. Although 5 or 8 additional damage may not seem much, remember that these numbers are doubled or tripled in wrath or divinity stances respectively. Furthermore, any multi hit or aoe attacks benefit greatly from this card. Perhaps the best example of this is ragnarok. Since the effect persists over multiple turns, it is possible to play Wreath of flame and only play an attack on a turn when you have entered wrath or divinity. Be aware that this is difficult to pull off with wrath cards such as tantrum and eruption, since the buff will be consumed before you have entered the stance. Outside of these uses, Wreath of Flame is worse than just drafting a standard attack, since if you draw a hand full of skills you might not be able to finish off an opponent where even a strike would have done the job.
